title: Information System Security Officer (ISSO)
description:
Torch Technologies

Thank you for your interest in employment with Torch Technologies. We are a 100% employee-owned, Certified Great Place To Work and named Best Places to Work in Huntsville/Madison County, headquartered in Huntsville, AL. Our team provides superior research, development, and engineering services to the Federal Government and Department of War. As one of the nation’s top 100 defense companies, the services we provide directly support the men and women who serve our country. Our corporate mission sums up the pride our employee-owners take in the work we do: “Lighting the Pathway of Freedom”. And, as a Certified Evergreen ESOP, we have made the commitment to grow and sustain our company for the next 100 years! Come grow with us!

Torch Technologies is seeking an Information System Security Officer. (ISSO) to join their team at Eglin AFB, FL.


Responsibilities:

  • Ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of classified Information Systems (IS) and data using Air Force approved network engineering practices, information security standards, and approved industry best practices.
  • Independently provide cybersecurity support for various test area systems, including real-time computers, standalone systems, and networked systems.
  • Evaluate approved new technologies prior to implementation within the organizational environment.
  • Independently provide cybersecurity support for application development, planning, network implementation, systems integration, communication support, computer-communication maintenance, asset management, and security controls.
  • Develop, maintain, and revise Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), System Security Plans (SSPs), and Approval to Operate (ATO) documentation.
  • Independently perform security scans using DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) to ensure systems security settings and patch levels are compliant.
  • Independently generate, collect, and preserve IS audit logs in accordance with the SSP and government customer requirements.
  • Independently monitor and document system changes in accordance with the Configuration Management Policy and the SSP.
  • Manage media control, including documentation and accountability of all media.
  • Support the Information System Security Manager (ISSM) in meeting their duties and responsibilities; assume ISSM responsibilities in the absence of the ISSM.

Required Qualifications:

  • U.S. Citizenship.
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in an applicable discipline. Degree requirements can be substituted with an applicable Associate’s degree and additional years of experience.
  • Must have a DoW 8140 Cyber Workforce Qualification certification (i.e., Security +).
  • Knowledge and expertise in Cybersecurity requirements, network technologies, and computer security as applied to Department of War (DoW) networks.
  • Experience developing SOPs and SSPs.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience performing all functions.
  • Must hold an Active Secret Security Clearance. (required to start)





Schedule: (M-F; 8-5)

Work Location: Onsite at Eglin AFB, FL

Travel: 0-10%

Relocation Assistance Available: No

Position Contingent Upon Award of Contract: No

title: Telecom Business Specialist - Network APIs
description:
Working at Infobip means being part of something truly global. With 75+ offices across six continents, we’re not just building technology — we’re shaping how more than 80% of the world connects and communicates.

As employees, we take pride in contributing to the world’s largest and only full-stack cloud communication platform. But it’s not just what we do, it’s how we do it: with curiosity, passion, and a whole lot of collaboration.

We operate with an AI-first mindset, embedding intelligent tools into our daily workflows to work smarter and more efficiently. Every role here benefits from and contributes to this approach.

If you're looking for meaningful work and challenges that grow you in a culture where people show up with purpose, this is your opportunity.

Let’s build what’s next, together.





What this role is all about

Telecom Business Specialist – Network APIs is an individual contributor role responsible for maintaining and increasing the company's revenue and gross profit through market coverage expansion & GTM partnerships. It does this by enabling, developing and managing connectivity with mobile network operators (MNOs) and aggregators for Infobip's Network APIs portfolio. These are CAMARA-standardized APIs within the GSMA Open Gateway programme, such as Number Verification, SIM Swap, KYC Match and Device Location.

An individual in this position acts as the commercial point of contact for operator and aggregator partners. They support and guide regional Operator Partnership teams by coordinating contracts, commercial negotiations, documentation and roadmap updates. Once connections go live, they make sure those connections run smoothly and stay profitable for everyone in the value chain.

You can find more information here:
- Network APIs:
- Mobile Identity:
- CAMARA APIs: What telecom operators need to know:

What will you do

Contract Management: Manage contracts with MNOs and aggregators, including revisions and coordination with internal and external stakeholders. Make sure terms are aligned with our Network APIs strategy. Collect and maintain the documentation required from operators and aggregators.

Commercial Terms and Pricing: Negotiate commercial terms, pricing and billing models with operators and aggregators. Work with Business Analysts to align pricing, so every connection contributes to the company's revenue and gross profit.

Market Analysis and Trends: Monitor global trends in Network APIs, GSMA Open Gateway and CAMARA. Make sure operators and aggregators share regular roadmap updates, and align our roadmap across markets so it reflects current operator capabilities and customer demand.

Commercial Support and Collaboration: Act as the link between HQ and regional Operator Partnership teams. Communicate global and regional updates, share global demand, initiate calls with operators, track contract and connection status, and set goals for Operator Partnership Managers in line with the Network APIs strategy. Hold regular calls with stakeholders, operators and aggregators.

Connection Management and Onboarding: Manage existing operator connections and support client onboarding together with the Technical Support team.

Process and Tracking: Keep Salesforce and internal tracking tables clean and up to date, so contract and connection status is always accurate. Actively look for areas to improve in existing processes and help refine them as the business grows.

Growth Path: As you build experience, you'll move toward more strategic, ecosystem-facing work. That includes taking part in relevant working groups, webinars and events, positioning and monetizing Network APIs through telco partnerships, and running discovery calls with MNOs. In those calls you'll position Infobip as a leading Network API expert and support operators in their Network API exposure, integration and go-to-market journey.

What makes you a strong fit


- 2+ years of working experience in a commercial, partner management or business operations role (telecom industry experience is an advantage).
- Degree in STEM, Economics, or relevant working experience.
- Customer and partner centric approach in all endeavors.
- Comfortable with contracts, commercial terms and pricing discussions.
- Organized and detail-oriented, with strong follow-through across many stakeholders and parallel tasks.
- Proactive drive to explore solutions and market trends.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written.
- Strong communication skills with both technical and non-technical audiences, internal and external.
- Experience with Salesforce is an advantage.
- Enjoy working in collaborative, fast paced environments.
- Goal driven and persistent.



Why you'll love it here • Financial rewards & recognition - A fair compensation aligned with your experience, industry, and market standards, performance-driven bonuses, regular reviews to support your growth and recognize your contributions, and a culture that values your impact. • Flexible work arrangements - We combine in-person collaboration with remote work and flexible working hours, because great ideas happen everywhere - and not always between 9 and 5. • ESOP (Employee Stock Ownership Plan) - As an Infobip employee, you’ll have the opportunity to share in our company’s success through stock options. • Work-life balance and Well-being - We offer time off when you need it, special leave days for life’s big moments, and a flexible hybrid work model tailored to local regulations. • Career mobility - Your career is a journey. With internal mobility, upskilling, and mentorship, we help you shape your path. • Professional development - Learning never stops. Onboarding, mentorship, and training programs help you grow - no matter where you start. • International mobility - Ready to take your career global? Explore short and long-term opportunities in our Hubs worldwide. While some benefits may vary by location, our goal remains the same: to support your growth, well-being, and success - wherever you are. 



Diversity drives connection

Infobip is built on diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and talents. We’re proud to be an equal-opportunity employer and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace.

No matter your race, gender, age, background, or identity — if you have the passion and skills to thrive, there’s a place for you here.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, national origin, citizenship, disability, veteran status or any other part of one's identity.

title: Lab Animal Technician 1
description:
When you join the growing BILH team, you're not just taking a job, you’re making a difference in people’s lives.

Job Summary: Provides daily husbandry care and maintenance required for the health and cleanliness of research animals and their housing facilities in accordance with established procedures and schedules which adhere to State and Federal regulations and accrediting agencies guidelines (AAALAC).
Reports to the Supervisor of the Animal Research Facility.<br><br>

Job Description:

Essential Responsibilities:
  1. Provides daily husbandry care to research animals according to department standard operating procedures, state and federal regulations and accrediting agency guidelines. These duties include but not limited to; providing clean sanitized caging material, fresh food and water and environmental enrichment on a scheduled and as needed basis.
  2. Monitors animal health and well being in assigned areas. Reports all signs of illness to the Supervisor immediately. Completes all required reporting documents and cage notification cards.
  3. Operates bio-safety cabinets, Animal Transfer Stations, chemical foamers, hydraulic lifts and specialized ventilated racks (if applicable). Reports all deficiencies immediately to the Supervisor.
  4. Houses newly arriving animal colonies according to department standard operating procedures. Ensures that orders match the posted incoming animal log and assigned cage cards. Reports errors immediately to the Supervisor.
  5. Monitors environmental parameters of assigned holding rooms for temperature and humidity. Records all information on the room log. Reports any deviations in acceptable ranges to the Supervisor immediately.
Required Qualifications:
  1. High School diploma or GED required .
  2. Certificate 1 preferred: Asst Laboratory Animal Tech, and Certificate 2 preferred: Laboratory Animal Technician
  3. 1-3 years related work experience required.
  4. One year of experience working with animals or in a lab animal environment.
  5. Must be able to follow detailed instruction and carry through with minimal supervision. Must be able to work well as part of a team.
  6. Must not be overly allergic to animals so as to affect ability to work with laboratory animals.
  7. Basic familiarity with computers. Ability to navigate at a basic level within web-based applications.
Preferred Qualifications:
  1. Knowledge of routine rodent handling/restraint and technical procedures.
  2. Previous work experience with laboratory animals.
Competencies:
  1. Written Communications: Ability to read, and write in English in order to understand basic safety instructions and take direction from supervisors; communicate effectively with patients, families and other medical center staff; and respond to basic questions.
  2. Oral Communications: Ability to understand spoken English in order to follow basic safety instructions and take direction from supervisors; communicate effectively in basic English with patients, families and medical center staff in response to routine questions.
  3. Knowledge: Ability to demonstrate basic knowledge of fundamental concepts, practices and procedures with the ability to use them in routine situations. Specialized knowledge not required.
  4. Team Work: Ability to interact respectfully with other employees, professional staff and/or external contacts to offer ideas, identify issues, obtain information or deliver services.
  5. Customer Service: Ability to demonstrate a positive attitude and respond to requests in a timely and respectful manner.

Physical Nature of the Job:
Medium work: Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally and or up to 20 pounds of force frequently. Job is physical in nature and employee needs to stand and/or move around through the majority of their shift.

Pay Range:

$19.23 - $24.04

The pay range listed for this position is the base hourly wage range the organization reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for this position at this time. Actual compensation is determined based on several factors, that may include seniority, education, training, relevant experience, relevant certifications, geography of work location, job responsibilities, or other applicable factors permissible by law. Compensation may exceed the base hourly rate depending on shift differentials, call pay, premium pay, overtime pay, and other additional pay practices, as applicable to the position and in accordance with the law.

title: Transplant Coordinator I
description:
Title: Transplant Coordinator I


Are you ready to save a life?

Do you want to be the person that makes the miracle of organ donation a reality? Do you want to turn tragedy into hope and healing? This is what we do every single day and we think you have what it takes.

Join a team that combines the fulfillment of an amazing mission with incredible benefits. This is not just another job or listing on your resume. Simply put, this job will change you, just like organ, eye and tissue donation and transplantation changes the lives of donor families and recipients.

Every day, the Lifebanc team gets the opportunity to change lives forever. Become a part of our family as we work toward a world where everyone in need of an organ or tissue transplant receives the healing they deserve. Come be a life saver.


What is Lifebanc?

Lifebanc, is the federally designated organ, eye and tissue recovery organization that serves 20 counties in Northeast Ohio. Put simply, we facilitate and coordinate organ, eye and tissue donation and transplantation in our community and educate the public on the importance of our mission. Our vision is pursuing a future where organ, eye and tissue donation is embraced as an honor and personal responsibility. Our mission is to save and heal lives.

Position Description:

The Transplant Coordinator I position is responsible for the facilitation of the organ donation process by providing clinical support through donor evaluation, donor medical management, organ placement and recovery in compliance with CMS and AOPO standards.

Essential Functions:

• Under the direction of the Administrator on Call (AOC), conducts evaluation of organ referrals and collects information to assist in the determination of donor suitability to maximize donation opportunities as required by UNOS, CMS and AOPO standards and Lifebanc policies.

• Covers assigned shifts to assure adequate coverage on a 24-hour basis including nights, weekends, and holidays.

• Responds onsite to referring hospitals within service area within the specified timeframe.

• Reviews and evaluates the patient’s Electronic Medical Record (EMR), to assist in the determination of donation eligibility and suitability.

• Evaluates the patient’s neurological status, consulting with medical staff caring for the patient.

• Serves as a member of the healthcare team and assists the Family Support Coordinators (FSC) and Hospital Services Coordinator (HSC) to identify and approach the appropriate next of kin for organ and tissue donation in compliance with CMS and AOPO standards.

• Facilitates the coordination of the medical management of the donor, following established guidelines as well as medical director guidance to maintain adequate organ perfusion and oxygenation to maximize organ potential.

• Medically manages potential pediatric and adult neurologically deceased donors as outlined in Lifebanc’s Clinical Practice Guidelines.

• Demonstrates a thorough understanding of hemodynamics including respiratory and ventilator management, electrolyte management and fluid balance.

• Draws and/or assists in the donor blood collection for the donor evaluation.

• Participates in all physical donor management in the Lifebanc Donor Care facility (DCF) including but not limited to the collection of specimens, medication and blood administration and ventilator management.

• Ability to recognize and treat cardiac arrhythmias and lead resuscitation as needed.

• Communicates all donor information accurately and timely to ensure transplantation.

• Knowledge of National organ allocation policies and procedures.

• Arranges all logistics of recovery teams including the transportation for organ recovery and organs for transplant.

• Performs other job duties as assigned.

Education and Experience:

• Associate’s degree in nursing (ADN) with current license as a Registered Nurse (RN) with at least two years’ experience in a critical care setting or,

• Current state licensure as a Respiratory Therapist (RT) with at least two years’ experience in a critical care setting or,

• One year of OPO experience and successful completion of Lifebanc’s Professional Development Program “Transplant Coordinator Track” or,

• One year of OPO experience and successful completion of a master’s degree in Transplantation and Donation Sciences.

Certification and Licenses:

• Current state licensure as a Registered Nurse (RN) or current state licensure as a Respiratory Therapist (RT) if required for experience.

• BLS (Basic Life Support) and ACLS (Advanced Cardiac Life Support) required; certification must be approved by the American Heart Association (AHA) .

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

• Basic computer skills and working knowledge of basic equipment.

• Critical care experience to achieve hemodynamic stability in a potential organ donor as well as the ability demonstrate critical thinking to implement treatment to optimize donation.

• Ability to assume responsibility without direct supervision, multitask and to demonstrate effective decision making within the scope of assigned authority

• Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to interact and communicate effectively with a wide range of people, including medical staff, hospital personnel and donor families.

• Ability to represent the goals and plans of the organization in a professional manner.

• Ability to exercise discretion and sound judgement.

• Ability to collaborate with multiple members of the health care team to effectively manage a potential organ donor.

• Ability to produce accurate records both written and electronic.

• Ability to work independently from a remote location, office or hospital/DCU setting.

• Current valid driver’s license and automobile insurance.

Physical Requirements:

• Physical stamina, including the ability to function at full capacity for hours consecutively.

• Ability to lift amounts over 50 pounds and carry and move Lifebanc and hospital equipment.

• Ability to perform direct patient care and transfers, assisting hospital personnel.

Compensation and Benefits:

When you join Lifebanc you can expect competitive salaries and a great benefit package. Our benefits include health, dental and vision insurance, health savings account, dependent care flexible spending account, short and long-term disability, and life insurance. We also offer a generous paid time off program, 401(K) retirement plan, parental leave, on-site fitness facility, tuition reimbursement and more!

Lifebanc is committed to a workforce that is diverse, inclusive and equitable. We encourage qualified candidates to apply.

Associated Bank requires you to directly represent yourself and your own experiences during the recruiting and hiring process. Associated Bank conducts a thorough background check on all new hires.

About Our Internship Program

Your internship is more than a summer experience. It’s a chance to explore what’s next. During Associated Bank’s 12-week internship program, you’ll gain meaningful, hands-on experience and build real-world skills while exploring career possibilities and discovering where your interests and strengths could take you. You’ll grow your network and learn from mentors and colleagues across the organization, all while experiencing our culture, values and mission in action and discovering what it’s like to build your career at Associated Bank.

  • Prototype, build, and support the deployment of AI agents and workflows for Corporate & Commercial Banking use cases.
  • Collaborate with bankers and other end users to understand their work, identify opportunities, and develop practical AI solutions that address their needs.
  • Apply AI solutions to improve banker and portfolio manager experiences, streamline processes, and support business and revenue-generating opportunities.
  • Test and iterate on AI agents and workflows, learn from results, and continuously improve solutions based on user needs.
  • Explore ways AI can help bankers generate ideas, identify potential opportunities, and perform their work more effectively.
  • Build and deploy AI solutions in alignment with established governance requirements while gaining hands-on exposure to the application of AI within Corporate & Commercial Banking.
  • Follow company policies, procedures, and confidentiality guidelines, and complete additional duties as assigned.

Education & Experience

Required

  • Bachelor's Degree student with sophomore, junior or senior standing at time of internship start date; must not have graduated prior to internship start date.

Preferred

  • Hands-on experience building, prototyping, or deploying AI agents or workflows.
  • Experience using AI tools to solve real-world problems.
  • Exposure to AI development tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, or similar tools.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

At Associated Bank, you’ll be part of a supportive, growth-focused team that values your contributions and invests in your development. We offer meaningful career paths, community engagement opportunities, and a culture built on respect and teamwork. Apply today to make an impact in your community and grow your career with us!


We welcome and encourage applications from all qualified parties, including but not limited to people returning to the workforce, people with disabilities, those without a college degree, and veterans or those with military experience.


In addition to core traditional benefits, we take pride in offering benefits for every stage of life.

  • Retirement savings including both 401(k) and Pension plans.
  • Paid time off to volunteer in your community.
  • Opportunities to connect with others through our diversity-focused Colleague Resource Groups.
  • Competitive salaries with professional development and advancement opportunities.
  • Bonus benefits including well-being programs and incentives, parental leave, an employee stock purchase plan, military benefits and much more.
  • Personal banking, loan, investment and insurance benefits.

Associated Bank serves more than 120 communities throughout Wisconsin, Illinois, Minnesota, and Missouri and we consider our colleagues critical to our continued success. See why our colleagues continually vote us a best place to work in the Midwest. Join our community on Facebook, LinkedIn and X.


Artificial Intelligence Statement


To support our recruiting process, we may use artificial intelligence ("AI") or automated technologies to collect, organize, sort, and analyze information submitted by applicants. title: GIS Specialist
description:
Summary

Responsible for creating, maintaining, updating, analyzing, and providing quality control of Engineering Geographic Information System (GIS) data and related infrastructure records. Supports Engineering operations by integrating approved plans, record/as-built drawings, plats, easements, project records, CAD data, and other engineering information into the City's GIS environment.

Provides GIS mapping, data maintenance, engineering records research, spatial analysis, and technical support to Engineering staff, other City departments, consultants, contractors, and the public. Assignments and projects may be performed independently or collaboratively as part of the Engineering GIS team, project teams, or cross-departmental teams, depending on the scope and requirements of the work.


Pay Range: $56,930-$64,854 (Depending on qualifications and experience)

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

1) Create, maintain, edit, and perform quality control of Engineering GIS datasets, including water, sanitary sewer, storm drainage, streets, pavement, project information, easements, right-of-way, subdivision, parcel, and other infrastructure or special-purpose GIS data.

2) Review and interpret approved engineering plans, construction drawings, record/as-built drawings, plats, surveys, easements, legal documents, CAD files, and other engineering records to accurately create and update GIS features and attributes.

3) Maintain GIS information related to new construction and completed Capital Improvement Projects (CIP), including project boundaries, project numbers, infrastructure improvements, record drawings, and related project information.

4) Research historical Engineering records, plans, project numbers, plats, easements, and record drawings to support Engineering Records Requests (ERR), internal requests, consultants, contractors, other City departments, and public information needs.

5) Perform GIS data quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC), identify spatial and attribute discrepancies, research source information, and make or coordinate necessary corrections to maintain data accuracy and integrity.

6) Create maps, exhibits, reports, data extracts, and other GIS products for Engineering staff, City management, Survey, Water Utilities, Streets, Planning, CIP, consultants, contractors, and other users.

7) Maintain and support GIS data used by Cityworks and other Engineering or asset-management workflows, including incorporating field changes, work-order information, completed construction, and infrastructure updates into GIS.

8) Assist with the development, maintenance, and support of ArcGIS Enterprise and ArcGIS Online content, including web maps, feature services, editing applications, dashboards, Experience Builder applications, Instant Apps, and other GIS solutions.

9) Work with CAD, MicroStation, AutoCAD, GPS/GNSS, spreadsheets, databases, and other engineering information sources to convert, integrate, georeference, and maintain information within GIS.

10) Perform spatial and attribute queries, geoprocessing, data conversion, georeferencing, and basic GIS analysis to support Engineering projects and operational needs.

11) Assist with GIS workflow improvements and automation using available GIS tools such as ModelBuilder, Arcade, Python/ArcPy, or similar technologies, as appropriate.

12) Maintain GIS documentation, metadata, procedures, data standards, and established Engineering GIS workflows to ensure consistency and continuity of information.

13) Coordinate GIS information and data updates with Engineering, Water Utilities, Streets, Planning, Survey, IT GIS, CIP staff, consultants, contractors, and other stakeholders.

14) Keep current with GIS technology, software, data-management practices, and evolving geospatial tools applicable to municipal Engineering and infrastructure management.

15) Maintain and organize Engineering records within OnBase, including entering, indexing, classifying, filing, and linking engineering plans, record/as-built drawings, plats, easements, project documents, and related records according to established document structure, naming conventions, project numbers, and Engineering records-management procedures.

16) Perform assigned GIS, Engineering records, mapping, data-maintenance, research, and project-related work independently or as part of a team. Collaborate with Engineering staff, other City departments, consultants, contractors, and project teams as necessary to complete assignments and meet project objectives and deadlines.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Associate's degree in Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Geography, Geospatial Science, Engineering Technology, Civil Engineering Technology, Surveying, Planning, Computer Science/Information Systems, or a closely related field.
  • Two (2) years of related GIS, engineering GIS, municipal GIS, utility GIS, CAD, surveying, infrastructure data, or closely related technical experience.
  • Ability to read and interpret civil engineering plans, record drawings, plats, maps, and related technical documents.

Or an equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential functions of the job.

Preferred Qualifications

Education/ Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Geographic Information Systems, Geography, Geospatial Science, Engineering Technology, Civil Engineering Technology, Surveying, Planning, or a closely related field.
  • Two (2) or more years of professional GIS experience, preferably in municipal government, Engineering, Public Works, water/wastewater utilities, stormwater, transportation, surveying, or infrastructure management.
  • Experience maintaining enterprise GIS datasets and working with engineering plans, record drawings, plats, easements, CAD information, or infrastructure records.
  • Experience working in a multi-department municipal GIS environment.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Working knowledge of Geographic Information Systems principles, practices, and data-management concepts.
  • Working knowledge of ArcGIS Pro for GIS editing, data management, map production, geoprocessing, spatial analysis, and QA/QC.
  • Knowledge of ArcGIS Enterprise and ArcGIS Online, including web maps, feature services, editing applications, dashboards, and other web GIS products.
  • Knowledge of enterprise geodatabases, GIS feature classes, spatial and attribute relationships, coordinate systems, projections, and georeferencing.
  • Ability to create, edit, maintain, query, analyze, and validate GIS data.
  • Ability to read and interpret civil engineering plans, record/as-built drawings, plats, surveys, easements, legal descriptions, and construction documents.
  • General knowledge of municipal infrastructure, including water, sanitary sewer, storm drainage, streets, pavement, easements, right-of-way, and related Engineering assets.
  • General knowledge of surveying, construction, and engineering practices.
  • Working knowledge of CAD/GIS integration and familiarity with MicroStation and/or AutoCAD.
  • Familiarity with Cityworks, asset-management systems, document-management systems such as OnBase, and GPS/GNSS data is preferred.
  • Familiarity with GIS automation tools such as ModelBuilder, Arcade, Python/ArcPy, or similar technologies is preferred.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office/Microsoft 365, particularly Excel, Outlook, Teams, and related applications.
  • Ability to research historical records and combine information from engineering plans, GIS, databases, document-management systems, and other sources.
  • Ability to identify GIS data discrepancies, research the source of the issue, and determine appropriate corrective action.
  • Ability to manage multiple assignments, prioritize workload, maintain accurate documentation, and meet established deadlines.
  • Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with City staff, consultants, contractors, and the public.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team, including multidisciplinary and cross-departmental project teams.

Licenses and Certifications

  • Valid Class C Texas driver's license
  • GIS-related professional certifications or technical training are preferred but not required.

Physical Requirements / Work Environment

The work environment and physical demands described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The position is primarily performed in a typical office environment using computers, GIS software, engineering plans, maps, and other technical records. The employee may also perform field work as needed to support GIS data verification, infrastructure location, project research, GPS/GNSS data collection, and review of existing field conditions.


Field activities may require the employee to:

• Travel to project sites and various locations throughout the City;

• Walk over uneven terrain, construction areas, rights-of-way, easements, streets, drainage areas, and other outdoor locations;

• Stand or walk for extended periods during field verification activities;

• Bend, stoop, kneel, reach, and climb as necessary to observe or document infrastructure;

• Carry and operate GPS/GNSS equipment, tablets, measuring devices, plans, or other field equipment;

• Work outdoors in varying weather conditions;

• Work near streets, traffic, construction activities, utilities, drainage facilities, and other municipal infrastructure environments;

• Safely enter active project or construction areas when authorized and in accordance with applicable safety requirements; and

• Drive a City vehicle or personal vehicle, as authorized, to conduct field verification, research, or data collection.


The employee must be able to perform prolonged computer work and visually review detailed maps, engineering drawings, aerial imagery, GIS data, and technical documents.


Office and field assignments may be performed independently or as part of a team depending on the nature, complexity, and safety requirements of the project. The employee may work with Engineering staff, Survey, Water Utilities, Streets, Planning, IT GIS, CIP, consultants, contractors, or other project stakeholders to complete assigned work.

title: Surgical Recovery Coordinator II
description:
Are you ready to save or heal a life?

Do you want to be the person that makes the miracle of donation and transplantation a reality? Do you want to turn tragedy into hope and healing? This is what we do every single day and we think you have what it takes.

Join a team that combines the fulfillment of an amazing mission with incredible benefits. This is not just another job or listing on your resume. Simply put, this job will change you, just like organ, eye and tissue donation and transplantation changes the lives of donor families and recipients.

Every day, the Lifebanc team gets the opportunity to change lives forever. Become a part of our family as we work toward a world where everyone in need of an organ or tissue transplant receives the healing they deserve. Come be a life saver.


What is Lifebanc?

Lifebanc, is the federally designated organ, eye and tissue recovery organization that serves 20 counties in Northeast Ohio. Put simply, we facilitate and coordinate organ, eye and tissue donation and transplantation in our community and educate the public on the importance of our mission. Our vision is pursuing a future where organ, eye and tissue donation is embraced as an honor and personal responsibility. Our mission is to save and heal lives.


This position is a dual role that is responsible for providing organ preservation services to provide safe transplantable organs to those in need while meeting AOPO and UNOS standards. This position also fulfills the role and responsibility of a surgical technician for Lifebanc organ donor cases.

Essential Functions:

· Covers assigned shifts on the organ preservation call schedule to assure adequate and reliable coverage on a 24-hour basis including nights, weekends and holidays.

· Effectively communicates with transplant surgeons and coordinators to provide information pertinent to the scheduled organ recovery and the perfusion and preservation of organs.

· Provides on-site organ recovery and preservation support for organs to a variety of recovery surgeon teams.

· Performs organ preservation during organ recovery/procurement and when applicable, performs recovery of an organ for research.

· Responsible for preserving, packaging, and labeling of organs to be delivered for transplant.

· Responsible for cannulating kidneys, placing on pump, and monitoring function for transplant.

· Coordinates organ import or export (including delivering appropriate labs and organs).

· Assists the donor surgeons during the removal of organs as first assist.

· Documents pertinent organ preservation information thoroughly and accurately.

· Maintains designated working area, equipment and supplies, assuring sufficient availability of viable supplies.

· Provide assistance to the local transplants centers in facilitating the import process in compliance with UNOS and Lifebanc policies.

· Assist the local transplant center once an organ has been accepted, including running the local list, contacting local labs and preservation and arranging transportation.

· Complete appropriate import documentation.

· Prepares for organ recovery in the operating room at Lifebanc’s DCF and assists donor hospital in preparation when needed.

· Performs the job expectations of a surgical technician in the setting of an organ recovery.

· Prepares for the recovery procedure by ensuring proper supplies are available and setting up the sterile table, instruments, and equipment appropriate to the surgical procedure.

· Identify surgical instruments by name and knowing their use and application.

· Assists in the draping and preparation of the donor and donor specimens.

· Assures that all instrumentation is accounted for pre and post procedure.

· Demonstrates an understanding of the use of surgical equipment, including electrosurgical devices, suction devices, emergency cardiac equipment and slush machines.

· Demonstrates an expertise in aseptic technique and assures compliance of all OR personnel during all phases of the organ recovery.

· Demonstrates preparation for instrumentation post case to meet sterilization needs.

· Assists in the facilitation and the recovery of organs and/or tissues for research purposes.

· Performs other job duties as assigned.

Education and Experience:

· High school diploma required.

· Graduate of an accredited School of Surgical Technology with a minimum of one year of experience as a surgical technician or; one to two years of equivalent OPO industry experience.

· BLS required; certification must be approved by the American Heart Association (AHA).

Certifications and Licenses:

· CTP (Certified Transplant Preservationist) recommended within two years and maintained throughout employment with Lifebanc.

· CST (Certified Surgical Technician) preferred.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

· Knowledge and understanding of medical terminology.

· Knowledge of and skill in sterile technique.

· Knowledge of anatomy.

· Ability to work nights and weekends.

· Willing to fly in small aircraft, if applicable.

· Ability to assume responsibility and make decisions without direct supervision.

· Ability to work for greater than 24 hours at a given time.

· Ability to communicate in a professional manner with a wide range of people, including medical staff and hospital personnel.

· Current valid driver’s license and automobile insurance.

title: Country Manager Mexico
description:
Working at Infobip means being part of something truly global. With 75+ offices across six continents, we’re not just building technology — we’re shaping how more than 80% of the world connects and communicates.

As employees, we take pride in contributing to the world’s largest and only full-stack cloud communication platform. But it’s not just what we do, it’s how we do it: with curiosity, passion, and a whole lot of collaboration.

We operate with an AI-first mindset, embedding intelligent tools into our daily workflows to work smarter and more efficiently. Every role here benefits from and contributes to this approach.

If you're looking for meaningful work and challenges that grow you in a culture where people show up with purpose, this is your opportunity.

Let’s build what’s next, together.

You will also drive growth in your market by exploring partnerships with local telecoms and communication channels, and by leading and developing the sales team in the country. You will represent Infobip's expertise, values, and reputation with customers, authorities, and industry groups.

title: Chief Automation and Digital Solutions Architect
description:
Torch Technologies

Thank you for your interest in employment with Torch Technologies. We are a 100% employee-owned, Certified Great Place To Work and named Best Places to Work in Huntsville/Madison County, headquartered in Huntsville, AL. Our team provides superior research, development, and engineering services to the Federal Government and Department of War. As one of the nation’s top 100 defense companies, the services we provide directly support the men and women who serve our country. Our corporate mission sums up the pride our employee-owners take in the work we do: “Lighting the Pathway of Freedom”. And, as a Certified Evergreen ESOP, we have made the commitment to grow and sustain our company for the next 100 years! Come grow with us!

Torch Technologies is seeking a highly experienced Chief Automation and Digital Solutions Architect to serve as the senior technical advisor and chief developer for enterprise automation, digital modernization, and data-centric solution engineering supporting the Eglin Research Site (ERS).

The successful candidate will lead the design, development, integration, and sustainment of secure, scalable, mission-aligned digital solutions that improve workforce efficiency, data quality, business-process execution, and operational readiness. This role requires demonstrated expertise in enterprise database engineering, workflow automation, Microsoft Power Platform development, application architecture, cybersecurity, and technical team leadership within complex United States Air Force (USAF), Department of War (DoW), or comparable enterprise environments.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Enterprise Automation, Innovation, and Digital Solutions

- Serve as the Chief Developer and senior technical advisor for enterprise automation, digital modernization, data-centric solution engineering, and associated technical architecture.

- Engage directly with senior leaders, mission owners, functional organizations, and cross-functional stakeholders to identify operational challenges, gather requirements, and translate needs into actionable data-driven business solutions.

- Lead the design and implementation of scalable digital products, automated workflows, data pipelines, dashboards, applications, and integrated enterprise services.

- Establish and promote technical standards, reusable design patterns, development practices, and governance processes for enterprise automation solutions.

- Independently lead solution discovery, requirements refinement, architecture design, technical execution, stakeholder engagement, and continuous improvement activities with minimal oversight.

- Assess evolving mission requirements and recommend modernization opportunities that improve usability, efficiency, readiness, resilience, and data-informed decision-making.

Enterprise Database Engineering and Data Architecture

- Architect, oversee, develop, and sustain advanced enterprise database solutions using Structured Query Language (SQL), relational data-modeling principles, Microsoft Dataverse, and enterprise data-assurance practices.

- Design secure and maintainable database schemas, data models, data-integration patterns, and data-quality controls.

- Develop and optimize data pipelines that support automated personnel, equipment, workflow-management, and mission-support capabilities.

- Ensure data solutions support appropriate data integrity, availability, traceability, access control, and lifecycle-management requirements.

- Identify database performance, integration, data-quality, and sustainability issues and develop corrective recommendations.

Power Platform and Application Development Leadership

- Lead enterprise-scale application and automation development using Microsoft Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI, Microsoft Dataverse, Azure services, and RESTful Application Programming Interface (API) integrations.

- Develop and oversee custom business logic, user interfaces, workflow automations, approval processes, notifications, dashboards, reporting tools, and integrated data solutions.

- Apply modern programming and scripting capabilities as needed, including JavaScript, TypeScript, C, JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), and related technologies.

- Develop technical approaches that enable secure interoperability among enterprise applications, data sources, APIs, cloud services, and mission-support systems.

- Guide application lifecycle practices from requirements definition and design through development, testing, deployment, sustainment, and retirement.

Cybersecure Architecture and Application Lifecycle Management

- Advise leadership and technical teams on secure system architecture, identity and authentication, access management, application security, and cybersecurity best practices.

- Support Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) practices, including source control, environment management, release planning, change control, testing, documentation, and sustainment.

- Ensure automation and digital solutions are designed and implemented in accordance with applicable USAF, DoW, customer, and enterprise security requirements.

- Identify, document, track, and mitigate technical risks, security concerns, integration dependencies, and potential single points of failure.

- Promote secure-by-design and data-protection principles throughout the solution-development lifecycle.

Technical Leadership, Collaboration, and Documentation

- Provide strategic technical direction, mentorship, structured development, and quality oversight to developers, automation specialists, network engineers, cybersecurity personnel, and other technical team members.

- Build effective working relationships among mission stakeholders, system owners, developers, cybersecurity teams, infrastructure teams, and enterprise IT organizations.

- Communicate technical concepts, implementation options, risks, timelines, dependencies, and recommendations to both technical and executive-level audiences.

- Maintain comprehensive documentation for development processes, solution architectures, application configurations, data schemas, workflows, interfaces, integration patterns, and operating procedures.

- Lead continuous evaluation and improvement of enterprise applications, workflows, data pipelines, and automation capabilities to remain aligned with mission needs and modernization objectives.

Required Qualifications

  • U.S.Citizenship.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity, information systems, software engineering, data engineering, information technology, or a related technical discipline.
  • Professional certifications relevant to enterprise architecture, cloud architecture, systems engineering, cybersecurity, program management, or agile delivery such as CISSP, CISM, or GSLC certifications or equivalent
  • Extensive experience in enterprise application development, workflow automation, digital modernization, data engineering, solution architecture, or comparable technical leadership roles.
  • Demonstrated experience leading multi-functional technical teams and coordinating complex modernization efforts across development, infrastructure, cybersecurity, and mission organizations.
  • Advanced experience designing and implementing relational databases, SQL queries, database schemas, data models, and data-quality processes.
  • Demonstrated experience with Microsoft Power Platform technologies, including Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI, and Microsoft Dataverse.
  • Experience designing, developing, or integrating RESTful APIs and enterprise application interfaces.
  • Proficiency with one or more modern programming or scripting languages, such as JavaScript, TypeScript, C, or similar technologies.
  • Knowledge of Azure services, cloud-based application architecture, identity and authentication concepts, and secure application-development practices.
  • Experience applying ALM, source control, release management, testing, change control, and documentation practices to enterprise applications.
  • Ability to independently gather requirements, develop solution approaches, manage stakeholder expectations, and execute technical work with minimal supervision.
  • Strong written, verbal, technical briefing, and stakeholder-engagement skills.
  • Ability to meet applicable customer access, security, onsite-work, and mission-support requirements.
  • Must be able to obtain/maintain an Active Secret Security Clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity, information systems, software engineering, data science, cybersecurity, or a related field.
  • Experience supporting USAF, Department of War, federal, defense, research and development, or similarly mission-critical environments.
  • Experience implementing enterprise governance for low-code/no-code platforms and citizen-development ecosystems.
  • Experience with DevSecOps, agile software delivery, infrastructure as code, cloud integration, API management, or enterprise data platforms.
  • Experience developing automation solutions for personnel management, equipment management, workflow tracking, asset management, readiness reporting, or business-process modernization.
  • Experience with enterprise reporting, dashboard development, data visualization, performance metrics, and executive decision-support products.
  • Experience developing technical standards, solution patterns, development playbooks, or governance processes for enterprise automation portfolios.

Key Competencies

  • Enterprise automation and digital modernization
  • Microsoft Power Platform architecture and development
  • Database engineering and SQL
  • Microsoft Dataverse and relational data modeling
  • Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power BI
  • Azure services and RESTful API integration
  • Application Lifecycle Management and DevSecOps practices

title: 2nd Shift Direct Care
description:
Position Summary

As a Residential Support Specialist, you will provide a supportive and safe environment in community residential settings within MHA’s ICL (Integrated Community Living) department. This role involves traveling to different program locations based on staffing needs, offering flexibility while providing consistent support across the department. You will help foster growth, independence, and community engagement for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities or autism. You will support individuals with daily living activities, personal goals, and participation in their communities while promoting dignity, choice, and independence.

Pay Range: $19 - $21 an hour

Open Shift: Mon 4p-11p, Tues & Wed 3p-11p, Sat & Sun 3p-11p (37 hours)

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide respectful, person-centered support to participants in daily living activities, personal care, and skill development.
  • Promote community integration by facilitating access to transportation, social activities, and external resources.
  • Support participants' health needs, including medication administration (per MAP standards), appointment scheduling, and monitoring overall wellbeing.
  • Assist with financial skills and money management, maintaining accurate documentation of all expenditures.
  • Respond to emergencies and crisis situations appropriately, following agency protocols and communicating with supervisors.
  • Advocate for participants and help them build self-advocacy skills; serve as a liaison with families, providers, and community supports.
  • Contribute to the development and implementation of Individual Service Plans (ISPs), documenting progress and participation.
  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation, including daily logs, incident reports, and health records.
  • Promote a safe environment by following all safety procedures, assisting with emergency drills, and identifying potential hazards.
  • Collaborate effectively with team members, attend training, maintain certifications (MAP, CPR, First Aid), and actively participate in meetings and supervision.

About Integration & Community Living (ICL)

The Integration & Community Living (ICL) program supports individuals with developmental disabilities and brain injuries in living independently and meaningfully in the community. In partnership with the Department of Developmental Services (DDS), ICL provides person-centered residential and outreach services across Western Massachusetts. With over 60 years of experience, MHA helps individuals transition from institutional settings into homes where they can grow, make choices, and fully participate in community life. Services range from supported and shared living to emergency respite and privately funded care, all designed to promote independence, dignity, and connection.

Equal Opportunity Statement

The Mental Health Association is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Requirements

  • Valid driver’s license and an acceptable driving record.
  • Adaptability to participants' changing needs.
  • Provide personal care, including assistance with bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, and mobility.
  • Ability to pass and maintain certifications in medication administration (MAP), CPR, and First Aid.
  • Must be at least 18 years old.
  • High school diploma or GED required; college degree in human services or a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of six months of relevant experience; experience working with individuals with mental health, intellectual and developmental disabilities, or autism is preferred.

Benefits

  • Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
  • Retirement Plan (403B, IRA)
  • Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick & Public Holidays)
  • Family Leave (Maternity, Paternity)
  • Long Term Disability
  • $19-21 an hour

title: Manager of Family Services
description:
Title: Manager of Family Services

Are you ready to save or heal a life?

Do you want to be the person that makes the miracle of donation and transplantation a reality? Do you want to turn tragedy into hope and healing? This is what we do every single day and we think you have what it takes.

Join a team that combines the fulfillment of an amazing mission with incredible benefits. This is not just another job or listing on your resume. Simply put, this job will change you, just like organ, eye and tissue donation and transplantation changes the lives of donor families and recipients.

Every day, the Lifebanc team gets the opportunity to change lives forever. Become a part of our family as we work toward a world where everyone in need of an organ or tissue transplant receives the healing they deserve. Come be a life saver.

What is Lifebanc?

Lifebanc, is the federally designated organ, eye and tissue recovery organization that serves 20 counties in Northeast Ohio. Put simply, we facilitate and coordinate organ, eye and tissue donation and transplantation in our community and educate the public on the importance of our mission. Our vision is pursuing a future where organ, eye and tissue donation is embraced as an honor and personal responsibility. Our mission is to save and heal lives.


Job Summary:

This position is responsible for providing supervision and leadership in the operational activities of the family support department to ensure donor decisions are supported and advocacy for donation opportunity is maintained within our community. This position will hold the Family Services responsible for obtaining yearly departmental KPIs and metrics set by the organization. As part of the Lifebanc leadership team, the Manager of Family Services is also responsible for fostering an organizational culture that is based on collaboration, support, and constructive feedback, enabling the organization to uphold our core values (service, teamwork, integrity, commitment, innovation, and quality).

Essential Functions:

· Provide direct supervision and leadership to Family Services Coordinators.

· Manages and coaches the Family Services Coordinators and clinical staff (as needed) in the approaches with the appropriate next of kin for organ, tissue and eye (O/T/E) donation.

· Promotes a culture of high performance and continuous improvement that values learning and a commitment to quality.

· Manages all aspects of the employment cycle (interview, onboard, training, discipline, performance management and offboarding).

· Works collaboratively with quality team to review audits and address deficiencies when noted.

· Participates with the health care team during end-of-life discussions with next of kin and/or significant others of potential and registered O/T/E if possible.

· Provides/seeks training to ensure staff is current on the required training for their roles quarterly.

· Ensures staff is providing informed authorization or disclosure to all donor families or agents.

· Performs monthly audits of reports to monitor department and individual goals.

· Maintain the ability to conduct a comprehensive medical social history interview with the next of kin, significant others and/or healthcare professionals of potential organ and tissue donors in compliance with CMS, AATB, FDA, and/or OPTN regulations and Lifebanc policies and provided support to donor families during the donation and recovery process.

· Completes the electronic Donor Risk Assessment Interview (DRAI) per Lifebanc policies and standards.

· Completes accurate reporting and documentation during shift change to ensure donor families remain supported.

· Oversees and provides corrections/review/completion of donor charts.

· Ensures team coverage and support for donor families that remain on-site at the hospital during the donor case.

· Ensures all staff completes mandatory consent training on a quarterly basis as well as annual competency as required by the role.

· Collaborates with key hospital staff members in real-time on all active referrals and/or cases as needed.

· Conducts individual/departmental huddles and meetings with staff.

· Ensures that all departmental responsibilities are completed correctly and in a timely manner.

· Supervises the donor family outcome letters and completes quarterly audit to ensure compliance.

· Assist in the development and day-to-day management of the departmental budget.

· Review and approve schedules, timecards, PTO requests, expense reports, and purchase orders for direct reports.

· Provide data and reporting support for departmental scorecards and strategic planning initiatives.

· Participate in policy review, development, and implementation of new procedures and guidelines.

· Performs other job duties as assigned.

Education and Experience:

· Bachelor’s degree in healthcare related fields and/or social work counseling from an accredited university and/or 5 years of Organ Procurement Organizational experience.

· Minimum 5 years’ work experience in professional health-care environment.

· Knowledge of regulations related to organ donation (Joint Commission, CMS, AATB, FDA, OPTN) required.

· Knowledge of organ, tissue and eye donation process required.

· 3 years of previous supervisory and/or administrative call experience.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

· Ability to assess situations and people and respond in a professional manner.

· Skill in presenting information to various audiences in an engaging and professional manner

· Ability to initiate interpersonal interaction with hospital staff and develop ongoing positive relationships

· Communicates job responsibilities and expectations to assure desired results.

· Ability to be on call and work extended hours, including weekends and holidays.

· Daily management and oversite of hospital system team, to include the identification of training and/or development opportunities that will assist the employee in achieving enhanced job performance and/or career objectives, review of personal goals and performance evaluation.

· Ensures the necessary compliance training is completed by the team.

· Constructively coaches and develops staff to seek optimal performance and promote effective leadership.

· Ability to travel to diverse locations to deliver services.

· Knowledge of hospital/facility infrastructure.

· Ability to prioritize based on emergent needs.

· Current valid drivers’ license and automobile insurance.

Physical Requirements:

•Ability to lift 25 pounds and sit or stand for extended periods of time.

Compensation and Benefits:

When you join Lifebanc you can expect competitive salaries and a great benefit package. Our benefits include health, dental and vision insurance, health savings account, dependent care flexible spending account, short-term disability, and life insurance. We also offer a generous paid time off program, 401(K) retirement plan, parental leave, on-site fitness facility, tuition reimbursement and more!

Lifebanc is committed to a workforce that is diverse, inclusive and equitable. We encourage qualified candidates to apply.

Med i bagagen har du sikkert en faglig uddannelse, men indgangsvinklen til jobbet, kan være mange, og erfaringen kan være både kort og lang, det vigtigste er, at vi er et godt match for hinanden, og du ønsker at bidrage med service i særklasse til Danmarks bedste kunder.

title: ADAS Systems Integration Engineer
description:
Overview


At Bertrandt, we are committed to delivering innovative engineering solutions that shape the future of mobility. We are seeking an experienced ADAS Systems Integration Engineer for Vehicle Development, Test & Validation of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and Automated Driving (AD) technologies for our customer in San Jose, California.


The successful candidate will play a key role in end-to-end feature development, software and hardware integration, vehicle commissioning, test execution, data analysis, and issue resolution. This position requires a hands-on engineer who is comfortable working with development vehicles, sensors, ECUs, measurement systems, and globally distributed engineering teams.


What You'll Do


ADAS Systems Development & Integration

  • Develop and refine ADAS/AD feature requirements, customer functions, and engineering specifications.
  • Support feature development throughout the entire lifecycle, from concept and integration through validation and release.
  • Create validation strategies, test plans, acceptance criteria, and scenario-based test catalogs.
  • Manage requirements and system interfaces across software, ECUs, sensors, vehicle networks, and supporting systems.
  • Apply systems engineering methodologies, including Automotive SPICE, Scrum, Functional Safety, and SOTIF practices.

Software Integration & Vehicle Commissioning

  • Integrate and deploy ADAS software, ECUs, sensors, and computing platforms into development vehicles.
  • Perform software flashing, configuration, calibration, startup, and system verification activities.
  • Maintain software baselines, vehicle configurations, release documentation, and compatibility records.
  • Troubleshoot software and hardware integration issues through diagnostics, log analysis, and communication trace evaluation.
  • Ensure development vehicles remain operational, reproducible, and ready for testing activities.

Vehicle Testing & Validation

  • Conduct vehicle-level, integration, regression, smoke, simulation, and road testing activities.
  • Execute local and cross-country test drives while maintaining safety and compliance requirements.
  • Verify vehicle readiness and troubleshoot issues identified during testing.
  • Document test results, defects, and corrective actions in internal systems.
  • Support release readiness assessments and validation signoff activities.


Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with software developers, systems engineers, validation teams, workshop personnel, and project managers.
  • Coordinate with international engineering teams, including engineering partners in Germany.
  • Provide technical guidance, troubleshooting support, and setup documentation.
  • Escalate safety, quality, schedule, and technical risks when necessary.

title: 2nd Shift Direct Care
description:
Position Summary

As a Residential Support Specialist, you will provide a supportive and safe environment in community residential settings within MHA’s ICL (Integrated Community Living) department. This role involves traveling to different program locations based on staffing needs, offering flexibility while providing consistent support across the department. You will help foster growth, independence, and community engagement for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities or autism. You will support individuals with daily living activities, personal goals, and participation in their communities while promoting dignity, choice, and independence.

Pay Range: $19-$21 an hour

Open Shift: Friday through Sunday 3p-11p (24 hours)

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide respectful, person-centered support to participants in daily living activities, personal care, and skill development.
  • Promote community integration by facilitating access to transportation, social activities, and external resources.
  • Support participants' health needs, including medication administration (per MAP standards), appointment scheduling, and monitoring overall wellbeing.
  • Assist with financial skills and money management, maintaining accurate documentation of all expenditures.
  • Respond to emergencies and crisis situations appropriately, following agency protocols and communicating with supervisors.
  • Advocate for participants and help them build self-advocacy skills; serve as a liaison with families, providers, and community supports.
  • Contribute to the development and implementation of Individual Service Plans (ISPs), documenting progress and participation.
  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation, including daily logs, incident reports, and health records.
  • Promote a safe environment by following all safety procedures, assisting with emergency drills, and identifying potential hazards.
  • Collaborate effectively with team members, attend training, maintain certifications (MAP, CPR, First Aid), and actively participate in meetings and supervision.

About Integration & Community Living (ICL)

The Integration & Community Living (ICL) program supports individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities or autism in living independently and meaningfully within their communities. In partnership with the Department of Developmental Services (DDS), ICL provides person-centered residential and outreach services throughout Western Massachusetts. With over 60 years of experience, MHA supports individuals in transitioning from institutional settings into homes where they can build skills, make choices, and actively participate in community life. Services include supported and shared living, emergency respite, and privately funded care, all designed to promote independence, dignity, and meaningful community connections.

Equal Opportunity Statement

The Mental Health Association is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Requirements

  • Valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record required.
  • Must maintain MAP, CPR, and First Aid certifications.
  • Must be at least 18 years.
  • High school diploma or GED required; college degree preferred.
  • At least six months’ experience with mental health, intellectual and developmental disabilities or autism is preferred.
  • Provide personal care, including assistance with bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, and mobility.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively with strong time management.
  • Effective verbal, written, computer, and organizational skills.
  • Flexibility to adapt to participants’ evolving needs.
  • Minimum of six months of relevant experience; experience working with individuals with mental health, intellectual and developmental disabilities, or autism is preferred.
