title: Senior Power Platform Engineer (Specialist) in DIGITAL ENTERPRISE SERVICES
description:
Location: Leeds or London

This role is a very exciting opportunity for a technical expert who can help deliver new products in the Power Platform ecosystem, enhance existing products, and mentor junior engineers on the team.

A Day in the Role

A typical day will start with a stand-up meeting alongside a multi-functional team of business analysts, testers, and fellow developers to review progress, blockers, and priorities. Next, you'll focus on some development for the current project you're assigned to; this could be building a complex Power Automate flow, enhancing an existing model-driven app or adding a new webpage to a Power Pages portal. There will be junior developers on the project team who you help to mentor, so you'll spend some time reviewing a piece of development they have completed and walking them through best practices for component reuse and a scalable design.

If you're in the office, you'll grab lunch in the canteen with some of your colleagues or go out for a walk around the city if the weather is nice.

In the afternoon you have a demo scheduled with partners of the project to show them an exciting piece of functionality that you designed.

Following this call, you finish documenting a best practice guide for solution and environment management. This is to help the wider team improve their knowledge and to ensure deployments are smooth and with minimal disruption.

Before logging off you'll update the backlog for your project and make some notes for a Power Apps security design meeting you have arranged for the following day.

Role Requirements

The senior Power Platform engineer is expected to provide technical expertise for the platforms and mentor junior developers on the team. The role requires good levels of development competency, experience in Agile and DevOps methodologies and the ability to inform best practice design. It will also require mentoring and peer reviewing along with advising on more complex operational incidents and problems.

Minimum Criteria

In terms of behaviours, we’re looking for someone who will bring the following to the team:

  • A high level of integrity, organisation and self-motivation with a desire for self-improvement
  • The ability to build effective working relationships with others and provide challenge where appropriate
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
  • Attention to detail with the ability to craft concise, informational user documentation
  • Researching and developing solutions that expand, modernise or improve the service and technology portfolios, automate IT operations, reduce costs or increase levels of service, to demonstrate technical ownership

Essential Criteria

We are interested in hearing from candidates who have the following capabilities:

  • Minimum of two years’ experience working with Microsoft D365 and Power Platform including Power Apps and Automate
  • In-depth experience of solution delivery using the full Software Development Lifecycle. This should include experience of working with the Agile and DevOps methodologies working with continuous delivery, automatic regression testing, TDD and monitoring
  • Experience in programming custom .NET workflows and plug-ins
  • Good knowledge of Power Pages and Power BI
  • Good knowledge of Azure cloud platform especially Logic Apps, Functions and Service Bus
  • Good knowledge of agile delivery methodologies as associated toolsets such as Jira
  • Good knowledge of CoPilot Studio and creating agents
  • Knowledge of CI/CD Pipelines and DevOps toolchains
  • Good .NET and C# skills
  • Good JavaScript skills
  • Knowledge of ITIL framework (understanding of Incident, Problem, Change)

Desirable Criteria

It would also be beneficial, but not necessary, to have some of the following:

  • Excellent .NET and C# skills
  • Excellent JavaScript skills
  • Knowledge of ITIL framework (understanding of Incident, Problem, Change)

Don't hesitate to apply if you don't meet all the criteria. We value diverse perspectives and believe that different backgrounds can contribute to our team's success.

How This Role Fits Into the Wider Bank

The senior Power Platform engineer works on the Power Platform team, within the Digital Enterprise Services Domain, of the DGCIO Central Services Division in Technology. Microsoft Power Platform is one of the Bank’s strategic tools with its importance being demonstrated through the segregation of the management of this technology to a dedicated team. The Power Platform Team manages the technical lifecycle of all instances of this bank wide licensed strategic tool, some 30 in all, across on premise and cloud infrastructure.

Our Approach to Inclusion

The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve.

At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public.

We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed.

From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team.

Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme. If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application.

The Bank values diversity and inclusion – we want to reflect the society we serve better, we want the best people to work for us and we want our workplace to be inclusive. We value all forms of diversity, including but not limited to age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion and sexual orientation. One way we support diversity and inclusion is through our staff run networks.

We are fully committed to having a diverse and inclusive working environment, and are open to considering how the role might be carried out with flexible working.

Salary and Benefits

We encourage flexible working, part-time working, and job-share arrangements. Part-time salary and benefits are pro-rated as appropriate.

London salary: £61,440 - £69,120

Leeds salary: £55,280 - £62,190

The benefits package currently includes:

- A non-contributory, career-average pension, currently providing a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of annual salary for every year worked. Through the flexible benefits programme, there is an option to increase accrual to 1/65th or decrease it to 1/105th in exchange for salary. The Bank may vary standard accrual rates and dial-up or dial-down rates, or withdraw the dial-up and dial-down options, at any time.

- A discretionary performance award based on the current award pool.

- An 8% benefits allowance, which can be taken as salary or used to purchase flexible benefits.

- 26 days’ annual leave, with the option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits.

- Private medical insurance and income protection.

Flexible Working

This role is open to flexible working patterns, which may include:

- Adapting your calendar to accommodate personal commitments, such as school runs, exercise, or appointments.

- Spreading the 50% in-office attendance expectation across the month to accommodate different working patterns.

- Working from abroad, subject to approval and policy.

National Security Vetting Process

Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice.

The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis.

The Application Process

This role closes on 10 November 2026 11:59pm.

Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process.

The assessment process will comprise of two interview stages.

title: Urgent Care Provider -(MD/DO/PA/NP)
description:
Provider (MD/DO/PA/NP) Job Description

Position Summary

The Provider is responsible for evaluating, diagnosing, and treating patients in a fast-paced urgent care environment while ensuring high-quality, efficient, and compassionate patient care. Providers are expected to support clinic workflow, maintain accurate documentation, follow company policies and clinical standards, and collaborate professionally with staff and leadership to support overall clinic operations and patient experience.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Evaluate, diagnose, and treat patients of all ages in an urgent care setting.
  • Order, review, and interpret labs, imaging, diagnostic testing, and medications as medically appropriate.
  • Perform procedures and treatments within scope of practice and clinical training.
  • Accurately complete EMR documentation, medical decision-making, treatment plans, and patient instructions in a timely manner.
  • Review and sign charts, lab results, imaging results, and clinical documentation as required.
  • Collaborate with Medical Assistants, front desk staff, leadership, and other providers to support patient flow and clinic efficiency.
  • Ensure all required consent forms, documentation, and orders are completed appropriately.
  • Follow HIPAA, OSHA, infection control, and clinic safety standards at all times.
  • Support clinic operations during high-volume periods and assist with workflow needs as necessary.
  • Communicate professionally and effectively with patients, coworkers, clinic leadership, and corporate staff.
  • Maintain compliance with company policies, clinical protocols, and regulatory standards.

Qualifications

  • Active Michigan license required.
  • NP, PA, MD, or DO.
  • Current BLS certification required.
  • DEA and DOT certification required and must be obtained within 30 days of hire.
  • Urgent care, emergency medicine, or family medicine experience preferred.
  • Strong clinical judgment, multitasking, communication, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Must have flexible availability throughout employment, including weekends, evenings, rotating clinic assignments, and/or shifts based on operational needs, which may include clinics operating until midnight.

Benefits

Eligible employees are offered:

Health Insurance

  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • 401(k)
  • Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • Opportunities for growth and advancement

Physical Requirements

  • This position may require extended periods of standing and walking, occasional bending and reaching, assisting patients when needed, and lifting/moving up to 25 pounds. Reasonable accommodations are available in accordance with applicable law.

This job description is intended to describe the general nature of the position and may not include all duties and responsibilities. Responsibilities may be modified at any time based on operational and business needs.

Labcorp is seeking a Study Director - Ecotoxicology to join our team at Alconbury, near Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire.

title: Senior PA/Office Executive to Executive Director, International Directorate
description:
Work at the heart of the Bank of England's international agenda

We are looking for a highly organised, proactive and relationship-focused individual to join the Executive Director's Office in International Directorate at the Bank of England. This is a unique opportunity to work at the heart of a fast-paced and high-profile area of the Bank, supporting senior leaders whose work shapes the UK's engagement with international economic and financial policy.

This is an exciting time to join International Directorate. The Governor currently chairs the Financial Stability Board and the UK will hold the G20 Presidency in 2027 and G7 Presidency in 2028. You will have a front-row seat to some of the most important international policy discussions taking place across central banking, financial stability and global economic affairs.

You do not necessarily need to come from a traditional Personal Assistant background. We welcome applications from individuals who have developed strong organisational, coordination and stakeholder management skills in a variety of settings and are looking to bring those skills into a senior leadership support role.

About International Directorate

International Directorate helps maintain the safe economic and financial openness of the UK economy. We monitor global economic and financial developments, support the Bank's policymaking responsibilities and lead much of the Bank's engagement with international organisations such as the G7, G20, IMF, FSB and BIS.

The Directorate offers a unique opportunity to work on issues that matter to the UK and global economy, while building networks across the Bank and beyond.

Why join us?

This role offers:

  • Exposure to senior Bank leadership.
  • The opportunity to build a strong network across the Bank.
  • Insight into international economic and financial policy.
  • A varied and fast-paced working environment.
  • Excellent development opportunities and a potential route into a wide range of future careers at the Bank.

The role

Working closely with the Executive Director, Private Secretary and wider office team, you'll play a key role in ensuring the smooth running of the Executive Director's Office.

You will:

  • Manage a complex and fast-moving diary, helping ensure priorities are effectively balanced.
  • Coordinate meetings, briefings, papers, travel and key engagements.
  • Build strong relationships across the Bank and with external stakeholders.
  • Support communication and information flow across the Directorate.
  • Anticipate issues and help find practical solutions before they become problems.
  • Handle sensitive information with discretion and sound judgement.
  • Work collaboratively with colleagues to create an efficient, supportive and inclusive office environment.

Role requirements:

Minimum criteria

  • Strong organisational, prioritisation and time management skills, with the ability to work in a structured way to a high standard under pressure.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks, issues and stakeholders simultaneously, quickly and effectively.
  • Ability to be part of, and work in, a strong team environment, displaying enthusiasm, reliability and flexibility, and being willing and able to take on new challenges.
  • Experience of being a self-starter who can operate proactively with limited guidance, using their own initiative.
  • Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with a high degree of discretion, maintaining confidentiality at all times.
  • High level of accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Curiosity and a willingness to embrace new technologies and ways of working to improve efficiency and effectiveness.
  • Some experience of managing or helping to set the workload of other staff.

Essential criteria

  • Experience of managing or coordinating multiple, complex priorities simultaneously.
  • Ability to build and sustain strong working relationships and networks, with excellent interpersonal skills and the confidence to deal with senior internal and external stakeholders, delivering a high level of service.
  • Track record of operating in a busy environment where organisational skills, planning and attention to detail were critical to success.
  • Evidence of learning quickly, adapting to new situations and taking on unfamiliar challenges.

Desirable criteria

  • Experience supporting senior leaders or leadership teams.
  • Experience coordinating complex diaries, meetings, events or projects.
  • Experience working in a large, complex organisation.

We recognise that successful candidates may come from a range of professional backgrounds. This role would suit someone who enjoys bringing order to complexity, building strong relationships and helping senior leaders operate at their best. Whether your experience comes from executive support, operations, project coordination, stakeholder engagement or another fast-paced environment, if you are highly organised, proactive and keen to develop your career at the Bank, we'd love to hear from you!

Our Approach to Inclusion

The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve.

At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public.

We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed.


From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team.

Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme. If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application.

Salary and Benefits Information

We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate.

Salary - £33,600 - £37,800 per annum

In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below:

  • Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time.
  • A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool.
  • An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits.
  • 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits.
  • Private medical insurance and income protection.

National Security Vetting Process

Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice.

The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis.

The Application Process

Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process.

This role closes at 23:59 on 03 November 2026.


Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

Full Time

Warren, OH

Ultium Cells, LLC. manufactures battery cells used in electric cars and other electric vehicles in a joint venture between LG Energy Solution, Ltd., and General Motors. Our mission is to ensure the seamless storage and transport of materials, thereby supporting stable and efficient production processes. We are seeking passionate and driven individuals to join our team and contribute to the continued growth and innovation of our logistics operations.

title: AI Technical Lead
description:
Your Journey at Crowe Starts Here:

At Crowe, you can build a meaningful and rewarding career. With real flexibility to balance work with life moments, you’re trusted to deliver results and make an impact. We embrace you for who you are, care for your well-being, and nurture your career. Everyone has equitable access to opportunities for career growth and leadership. Over our 80-year history, delivering excellent service through innovation has been a core part of our DNA across our audit, tax, and consulting groups. That’s why we continuously invest in innovative ideas, such as AI-enabled insights and technology-powered solutions, to enhance our services. Join us at Crowe and embark on a career where you can help shape the future of our industry.

Job Description:

About Crowe AI

Everything we do is about making the future of human work more purposeful. We do this by leveraging state-of-the-art machine learning, generative AI, modern architectures, and industry experts to create AI-powered solutions that transform the way we do business.

Our world-class AI and ML professionals give Crowe the ability to capture and harness the power of data. A combination of AI and Machine Learning Engineers and AI Platform and Infrastructure Engineers create and deploy AI functionality to solve complex problems. We focus on building scalable AI solutions, based on rigorous data exploration, validation via proof-of-concept buildout, and close partnership with subject matter experts across business areas.

The future is powered by AI, come build it with us.


Role Overview

Crowe’s Studio team is seeking an AI Tech Lead to serve as a hands-on technical leader for the design, development, and lifecycle management of AI agents that accelerate the delivery of Crowe’s Audit services. This role is built around Crowe’s forward deployed engineer (FDE) model: rather than sitting above a project as a traditional program manager, this person sits with Audit practitioners, learns the workflow, designs the agent as it is built, and owns the outcome end to end. The goal is to establish the technical patterns, Skills-based architecture, and engineering practices needed to support a growing portfolio of agents. As that portfolio grows, the role is expected to grow into leading a small team as an engineering manager with full-stack engineers who each own a slice of the roadmap.


Key Responsibilities

Delivery of Audit AI Agents

  • Own the design, development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of AI agents and agent-assisted workflows that accelerate the execution of common tasks across Crowe’s Audit practice.
  • Operate as a forward deployed engineer paired directly with an Audit SME — sitting with practitioners, learning the workflow firsthand, and designing the agent as it is built rather than from a static spec.
  • Remain hands-on in development: write, review, test, and maintain substantial Python codebases and the Skills, instructions, prompts, and supporting resources that define agent behavior.
  • Manage project scope, timelines, and stakeholder communication for the agents you own — balancing hands-on delivery with the planning, prioritization, and coordination expected of a senior technical lead.
  • Design and develop agents using a Skills-based architecture — modular, reusable capabilities that can be efficiently discovered, invoked, tested, maintained, and enhanced over time.
  • Serve as the technical authority for the agent layer, making key design and implementation decisions while partnering with architects and engineering teams to ensure alignment with the broader Audit technology ecosystem.
  • Implement and maintain monitoring, observability, and alerting for agents running in production, including trace-level visibility into agent reasoning and tool calls, to proactively detect, diagnose, and resolve issues.

Build and Scale the Engineering Capability

  • Establish reusable engineering patterns and development practices that let a growing portfolio of agents be developed, evaluated, deployed, supported, and enhanced sustainably.
  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines in Azure DevOps to automate testing, evaluation, and deployment of agents across environments.
  • As the portfolio grows, lead a small team of forward deployed engineers that advance the roadmap per the audit stakeholders they serve.
  • Participate in the development and evolution of agent evaluation strategies, including representative test cases, automated evaluators, regression testing, quantifiable accuracy metrics, and processes for identifying and addressing changes in agent behavior.
  • Mentor engineers and provide technical leadership, including code and design reviews, as the agent portfolio and supporting team grow.
  • Promote collaboration across the Audit BU and the broader Studio to surface opportunities, share reusable patterns, and avoid duplicated build effort.

Product Judgment

  • Think in terms of ROI, business case, and value pool for every initiative, defining and tracking KPIs to measure and communicate business impact; make product decisions directly alongside the SME rather than routing through a separate product owner.
  • Demonstrate a solutions-oriented approach: be proactive, identify solutions independently, initiate activities, and follow through to completion.
  • Leverage data and insights to shape and defend a point of view aligned to Audit’s business needs.
  • Communicate proficiently with both technical staff and business leaders, articulating complex ideas, strategies, and recommendations in terms each audience can act on.

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering experience developing, implementing, and supporting enterprise applications and services.
  • 5+ years of professional Python development experience, with a strong track record of building enterprise-grade applications and services.
  • Demonstrated ability to write clean, maintainable, modular, testable, and well-structured Python code designed for long-term support and scalability — production-grade software that does not create technical debt.
  • 1+ years of hands-on experience designing, developing, and productionizing AI agents or AI-assisted workflows using a major AI platform or model provider such as Microsoft, Anthropic, or OpenAI.
  • Hands-on experience developing agents using a Skills-based architecture, including authoring and maintaining Skills definitions, markdown-based instructions, supporting resources, and executable code used by agents.
  • Experience testing and evaluating AI systems, including automated evaluators, representative test cases, regression testing, and analysis of agent failure modes.
  • Demonstrated ability to embrace and advocate for AI-assisted software engineering practices, including the effective use of coding assistants (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot), automated testing, and design-time AI tools to accelerate solution design, improve quality, and enhance developer productivity.
  • Demonstrated project management experience — scoping, planning, and managing technical projects/initiatives end-to-end in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment — with a strong track record of proactive, independent problem-solving.
  • Experience providing technical leadership to software engineering teams, including mentoring engineers, conducting code and design reviews, and establishing engineering practices and standards.
  • Experience designing and deploying AI/ML solutions on major cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, and/or GCP), including the use of managed AI services, cloud-native integration patterns, scalable data architectures, and secure, enterprise-grade deployments. Azure experience preferred
  • Experience with Azure DevOps — including building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines — or a similar platform, and Git-based version control.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical work to non-technical business leaders and translate complex requirements into practical technical solutions alongside product managers, architects, and business stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Experience developing software or AI solutions for Audit, accounting, public accounting, financial services, or another regulated industry.
  • Proficiency with modern AI/ML frameworks, tools, and agent platforms (e.g. MCP, A2A, Microsoft Foundry, OpenAI Agent SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework, Claude SDK, LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Microsoft Copilot Studio, or equivalent). Knowledge of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), vector databases, embeddings, and techniques for grounding model outputs in enterprise data.
  • Experience delivering solutions with the Microsoft .NET stack, C#, and SQL Server.
  • Experience helping establish or scale an engineering capability, including defining development standards, reusable patterns, and practices that support a growing team and portfolio of production solutions.
  • Consulting, product management, investment banking, or startup experience that has developed strong commercial and product instincts.
  • Prior experience as a forward deployed engineer or similar embedded technical role, partnering directly with subject matter experts to design and build workflow software without a separate product-owner layer.
  • Demonstrated passion for sharing what you learn, whether by offering cross-training opportunities, giving internal team “lightning talks,” or by writing detailed comments on tickets when you close them.
  • Demonstrated curiosity and continuous learning mindset in Generative AI and applied machine learning, with an interest in staying current on emerging models, architectures, and techniques, including engaging with original research, technical papers, and pre-release concepts before they are broadly commercialized

title: Product Owner
description:

You will experience these qualities of passion, pride and aspiration in many ways — from a rich set of career development programs to support of community service projects to social events that foster fun and relationship building across our global community.

The Role

As a Product Owner within our Manufacturing & Supply Chain (MSC) organization, you will play a key role in defining and delivering software solutions that help customers optimize planning, scheduling, logistics, supply chain operations, and industrial workflows.

You will work closely with Product Management, Software Development, Architecture, Quality Engineering, and other stakeholders to maximize customer value through effective backlog management, feature definition, prioritization, and Agile execution

Your Impact

  • Work closely with Product Management, Software Development, Quality Engineering, and Architecture teams to define and deliver innovative Manufacturing & Supply Chain solutions.
  • Own and prioritize the team backlog to maximize customer and business value.
  • Translate complex customer requirements, operational workflows, and business processes into well-defined features, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
  • Collaborate with engineering teams to align product capabilities with technical strategy, architecture direction, and delivery objectives.
  • Drive feature decomposition and backlog readiness to support effective Agile planning and execution.
  • Participate actively in PI Planning, Backlog Refinement, Iteration Planning, Sprint Reviews, and other Agile ceremonies.
  • Manage feature priorities, dependencies, risks, and trade-offs across teams and stakeholders.
  • Validate delivered functionality against customer needs, business objectives, and acceptance criteria.
  • Partner with Product Management, Services, Support, Customer Success, and other stakeholders to ensure successful adoption of delivered capabilities.
  • Foster a culture of customer-centricity, continuous improvement, value delivery, and data-driven decision making.
  • Contribute ideas for product innovation, process improvements, and customer-focused solutions.
  • Continuously develop domain expertise in Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Optimization, Planning & Scheduling, and Industrial Software solutions.

What You'll Need

  • Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations Research, or a related technical field.
  • 8+ years of progressive experience in Product Ownership, Product Management, Business Analysis, Solution Consulting, or related product leadership roles.
  • 5+ years of experience working within Agile software development environments.
  • Proven experience working within SAFe or other scaled Agile frameworks, including ownership and management of product backlogs, prioritization activities, and feature planning.
  • Strong business and technical acumen with the ability to bridge customer needs and engineering solutions.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex business requirements and operational workflows into actionable software deliverables.
  • Experience defining features, user stories, acceptance criteria, and backlog priorities.
  • Experience collaborating effectively with Software Engineers, Architects, and Quality Engineering teams.
  • Strong communication, stakeholder management, facilitation, and collaboration skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence decisions and drive alignment across cross-functional teams.
  • Experience managing dependencies, priorities, and trade-offs in complex software delivery environments.
  • Understanding of Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Planning & Scheduling, Logistics, Optimization, Industrial Software, or Enterprise Applications is highly desirable.
  • Familiarity with optimization concepts, operational workflows, or decision-support systems is considered a strong asset.
  • SAFe Product Owner/Product Manager (POPM) certification is considered an asset.
  • Passion for delivering customer value through innovative products and experiences.
  • Willingness to learn, adapt, and continuously improve in a dynamic environment.

title: General Interdisciplinary Engineer- Journeyman
description:
Torch Technologies

Thank you for your interest in employment with Torch Technologies. We are a 100% employee-owned, Certified Great Place To Work and named Best Places to Work in Huntsville/Madison County, headquartered in Huntsville, AL. Our team provides superior research, development, and engineering services to the Federal Government and Department of War. Our corporate mission sums up the pride our employee-owners take in the work we do: “Lighting the Pathway of Freedom”. And, as a Certified Evergreen ESOP, we have made the commitment to grow and sustain our company for the next 100 years! Come grow with us!

Torch Technologies has an exciting opportunity for a General/Interdisciplinary Engineer providing support to the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center/Airborne Warning and Control System (AFLCMC/HBS/WIW). The Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) Division, has the collective Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC) mission responsibility to deliver airborne Battle Management Command & Control (BMC2) capabilities that support joint, allied, coalition, humanitarian, and homeland defense operations. Modernization efforts enable continued involvement with worldwide operations by revitalizing legacy mission systems, replacing aging computer architectures, integrating multi‑sensor data fusion, and improving global expeditionary readiness and availability. Additionally, the Division assists in the planned divestiture of the E‑3 platform and in shaping development of follow‑on capabilities for future airborne C2 systems.

This is a full time Hybrid position located at Tinker AFB, OK.


Duties include, but not limited to:

Design & Architectures

  • The Contractor shall provide engineering support in the design, operation, and sustainment of systems and components that cover tasks throughout the acquisition life cycle (requirements analysis through system disposal). Tasks may also include supporting Foreign Military Sales.
  • Conduct and support all engineering and technical activities required during the material solution analysis, technology, engineering, and manufacturing development, production and deployment, and operation and support phases of the systems acquisition process. Develop/prepare engineering and technical documentation inherently part of the activities listed above (e.g. Analysis of Alternatives (AoA), Systems Engineering Plan (SEP)…), systems review and analysis with written reporting, briefing, and artifact development as required for all of the technical specialty areas defined in this section; and the planning and execution of all necessary technical reviews, assessments, and interchange meetings (e.g. Critical Design Review(CDR), Manufacturing Readiness Assessment (MRA), Reliability Technical Interchange Meeting (TIM)) and associated artifacts (e.g. Critical Design Review entry and exit criteria).
  • Conduct systems architectural analyses to include system design/design feasibility and state-of-the-art assessment
  • Produce architectures, document planned and existing systems, determine deficiencies, develop alternatives, recommend solutions, and support development of a plan to implement the chosen solution per acquisition and sustainment system engineering processes. This may include traditional architecture development or Model Based Systems Engineering processes.
  • Track and ensure system architecture and interoperability requirements for the baselined system is maintained.
  • Detail operational requirements and functional interactions within the system and with other systems, considering life cycle costs, logistics supportability, human factors, et al, to determine if the basic building blocks of the system are defined in sufficient detail to support a development program effort.
  • Translate DoW user requirements into system requirements for designing, developing, testing and evaluating systems and subsystems using USAF and DoW approved acquisition methods.
  • Provide engineering analysis of system training, training equipment and simulator requirements; prepare technical documentation; and provide engineering evaluation of equipment and simulator designs.

Acquisition

  • Understand and implement robust DoW acquisition and sustainment systems engineering processes to address the life-cycle requirements of each product support area
  • Prepare and review program specifications for items, processes and materials. Develop and utilize analytical, simulation, MBSE and digital engineering analysis techniques to optimize system performance and/or system effectiveness; establish system sensitivities, define system parameters, evaluate hardware and validate flight test results in terms of overall system relationships and applications.
  • Develop, prepare, review, and integrate selected milestone review documentation, periodic reports, and certifications as identified in current DoW and AF acquisition policy.
  • Review, evaluate and monitor acquisition Contractor drawings for completeness, currency, technical accuracy and conformance to requirements, specifications, regulations and quality control to ensure compliance with ASME technical Data Package format and requirements.

Technical Management

  • Complete and support requirements definition and analysis, architecture design, implementation, integration, verification and validation, transition, decision analysis, requirements management, risk management, interface management, and configuration management
  • Facilitate the transfer of information, lessons learned and best practices across all customers and contractors serviced under this task order within constraints of proprietary rights
  • Perform market research and trade studies to assess current and future systems to ensure they that meet mission needs/requirements. Conduct, define and evaluate system cost, schedule, and technical performance. Perform reviews, studies (including root cause analysis), audits, evaluations and analyses and provide technical recommendations to the Government.
  • Conduct engineering performance, effectiveness, cost effectiveness, cost performance, life cycle cost, producibility, reliability and maintainability, risk and scheduling trade-off studies
  • Develop USAF approved Test and Evaluation Master Plans (TEMP), test plans and procedures, prepare test readiness reviews and associated test documentation using DoW and USAF standard processes, execute developmental tests and assist in operational test planning/execution, and evaluate tests in support of acquisition and sustainment programs.
  • Participate in integrated logistics support efforts, provisioning and source coding, maintenance data collection, technical order management, configuration management, evaluation of quality deficiency reports, and/or identification of alternate sources of supply for diminishing manufacturing/materiel sources preferred.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • U.S. Citizenship.
  • Bachelor’s Degree in a related field and 3 years of experience in the respective technical/professional discipline being performed, 3 of which must be in the DoW OR 7 years of directly related experience, 5 of which must be in the DoW.
  • Must have and maintain an Active Secret Clearance.

Technical Skills

  • Develop and prepare technical documentation recommending system and subsystem characteristics, including engineering analyses and corrective action plans.
  • Create management reports and technical presentations supporting planning, implementation, and sustainment activities.
  • Apply engineering theories, principles, and economy concepts to evaluate system performance, cost, risk, and life‑cycle considerations.
  • Perform requirements analysis, architecture development, integration, verification/validation, and configuration management across the acquisition life cycle.
  • Conduct trade studies, market research, root‑cause analyses, audits, evaluations, and technical reviews, providing recommendations to government stakeholders.
  • Support test planning and execution (TEMP development, test readiness reviews, developmental and operational test support).
  • Perform engineering performance assessments including cost‑effectiveness, producibility, reliability, maintainability, and scheduling trade‑off studies.
  • Utilize Microsoft Office Suite to produce documentation, reports, presentations, and analytical artifacts.
  • Collaborate across customers and contractor teams to facilitate information transfer, lessons learned, and best practices.

Interpersonal Skills

  • Strong communication skills for interfacing with program offices, government personnel, contractors, and cross‑functional engineering teams.
  • Self‑starter capable of working independently while following established processes and program guidelines.
  • Effective team collaborator able to coordinate across engineering, logistics, test, and acquisition disciplines.

Labcorp is seeking a Study Director – Analytical Chemistry to join our Environmental/Ecotoxicology team at Alconbury, near Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire

Job Responsibilities:

  • Perform the duties of a Study Director/Principal Investigator for studies allocated by Management

  • Ensure that test and control items have been suitably tested for identity, stability etc. and that all necessary technical data regarding known toxicity, hazards of the test item or related materials have been obtained from literature searches. To ensure that technical staff are aware of known hazards relating to a particular test item
  • Monitor the status of observations made during the study and ensure the responses are fully documented. Maintain an overview of the implication of these observations
  • Review all data to ensure its accuracy and that checking procedures have been observed compliant with Good Laboratory Practice and that suitable responses/actions are made following Quality Assurance Audit

Make interim decisions regarding necessary amendments, to document such changes and to agree them with the Study Sponsor. Communicate with the Sponsor and Departmental and Project Management as required with particular regard to problem areas which may affect completion date or content of the study
  • Inform the Sponsor of the results as soon as possible after the study completion date. Prepare draft and final reports ensuring the report is concisely and accurately written, reflects the raw data and includes all relevant information
  • Transfer all study data and reports to the Archive in a timely manner following the issue of the final report, in accordance with Company procedures and SOPs
  • Maintain computerised monitoring system for studies such that the information is up to date to enable study monitoring by their supervisors and other departments
  • Communicate with Ecotoxicology in the conduct of studies
  • Co-ordinate the supply of test vessels and equipment in conjunction with other members of staff thereby ensuring their availability for study start up
  • Contribute to the general management of the Analytical department in areas outside of that required as a Study Director
  • Travel as necessary, or to be available in-house to meet current and prospective sponsors to discuss existing and future studies
  • Keep up-to-date with trends in relevant analytical areas. Review specific topics as necessary so as to be able to discuss with Sponsors

  • Provide advice and support to internal and external customers relating to any study and non‑study related topics
  • Perform those duties of other members of staff absent due to sickness, holidays or training. Overtime may be required in response to work-load demands.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Degree in Chemistry

Additional Job Standards:

  • Significant experience within a Study Director role in Analytical Chemistry
  • Knowledge of GLP and regulatory guidelines
  • Knowledge of data interpretation and report writing for studies
  • Experience of customer service communication
  • Proficiency in project management skills
  • Ability to conduct literature review
  • Due to the remote location of this site, there are no public transport links available

We are looking for a Study Director is to ensure that studies are conducted to agreed schedules by liaising with key staff involved in study conduct and maintaining an awareness of all aspects of the studies ensuring that a Study Plan is prepared, approved and implemented. Informing the Sponsor of study progress and preparing study reports that accurately reflect the raw data obtained. Ensuring suitable levels of compliance of all laboratory data, documentation and procedures conducted within the department and satisfy the requirements of GLP and Company SOPs and provide advice and support to internal and external customers relating to study designs and regulatory issues, as required.

Labcorp is seeking a Director, Product Management (Women's Health, Pregnancy and Fertility) to join our team

  • Lead product and portfolio lifecycle strategy, forecasting, and roadmap development.

  • Partner with Marketing to support differentiation strategy and thought leadership priorities.

  • Use AI tools and agents to accelerate portfolio analysis, planning, and execution while maintaining accountability for decisions.

  • Bachelor’s degree.

  • 5 or more years’ experience in healthcare services business with knowledge of regulatory reimbursement environment.

  • Experience with diagnostics commercialization and regulatory pathways.

  • Forecasting & Pricing experience.
  • Experience applying AI to accelerate product-management workflows, business-case drafting, competitive and regulatory monitoring, forecasting input preparation, or launch-readiness coordination, with clear judgment about where AI adds value and where human expertise must lead.

  • Demonstrated ability to use AI-synthesized market, scientific, and competitive intelligence to strengthen portfolio decisions and cross-functional alignment, while treating AI output as a contributor to, never the source of, strategy.
  • Experience using AI to standardize artifacts, terminology, and handoffs across adjacent marketing disciplines (Product Management, Solution Marketing, Customer Marketing) to support consistent, cross-team execution.

  • Cross-functional leadership
  • Product lifecycle management & commercialization
  • Scientific and clinical fluency
  • Analytical and forecasting capability
  • Stakeholder influence

As the leader in global diagnostic services, Labcorp’s mission is to improve health and improve lives. Maintains a strong partnership with the BILH Credentials Verification Office (CVO), hospital and physician leadership, and other key stakeholders to support consistent, compliant, and efficient provider credentialing and Medical Staff operations across BILH.

Job Description:

Essential Duties & Responsibilities including but not limited to:

1. Provides direct leadership and oversight of the Medical Staff Services Department (MSSD) team, ensuring effective daily operations, consistent application of policies, staff development, performance monitoring, and a commitment to operational excellence.
2. Collaborates with the system Credentials Verification Office (CVO), Hospital Leadership, and Legal Counsel to support providers through the application process, ensuring timely appointment, reappointment, privileging, and management of credentialing expirables in compliance with Medical Staff Bylaws, Rules and Regulations, hospital policies, and applicable regulatory requirements, including those of The Joint Commission (TJC), the National Committee for Quality Assurance (NCQA), and state and federal agencies.
3. Oversees staff and ensures the timely and accurate credentialing, recredentialing, and privileging of providers affiliated with the hospital.
4. Manages and coordinates the timely submission of data and documentation for delegation audits by insurance plans, as applicable.
5. Ensures the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of provider data entered into the credentialing database by the MSSD staff.
6. Oversees and manages the maintenance and organization of electronic provider records in accordance with regulatory and organizational standards.
7. Partners with system and physician leadership to develop new clinical privilege forms or revise existing forms to reflect current practice and regulatory expectations.
8. Conducts regular team meetings to communicate updates, address concerns, and support team cohesion and performance.
9. Conducts regular staff meetings.
10. Responsible for recruiting, training, mentoring, and evaluating staff, as well as fostering their ongoing professional development.
11. Participates in the development and monitoring of the departmental budget, including variance reporting and resource planning.

12. Monitors departmental productivity and develops strategies to optimize operational effectiveness and efficiency.
13. Develops new policies and procedures, and oversees the routine review, revision, and enforcement of existing policies to ensure regulatory and organizational compliance.
14. Coordinates all aspects of assigned Medical Staff committee meetings—including the Credentials Committee, Medical Executive Committee, and Medical Staff Appointment Committee of the Board—ensuring accurate preparation of agendas, minutes, reports, and timely follow-up on actions.
15. Oversees the implementation, coordination, and management of the Focused Professional Practice Evaluation (FPPE) and Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE) processes.
16. Maintains current knowledge of and ensures compliance with all relevant regulatory and accreditation standards, including TJC/DNV, NCQA, CMS, and state and federal laws, as well as Medical Staff Bylaws and hospital policies.
17. Promotes a culture of excellence, professionalism, and customer service in all internal and external interactions and represents the organization positively in all external engagements.
18. Performs other related duties as assigned to support departmental and organizational goals.

Organizational Requirements:
1. Maintain strict adherence to the BILH Confidentiality policy.
2. Incorporate BILH Standards of Behavior and Guiding Principles into daily activities.
3. Comply with all Departmental Policies.
4. Comply with behavioral expectations of BILH.
5. Maintain courteous and effective interactions with colleagues, providers, and BILH leadership.
6. Demonstrate an understanding of the job description, performance expectations, and competency assessment.
7. Demonstrate a commitment toward meeting and exceeding the needs of our customers and consistently adheres to BILH customer service standards.
8. Participate in departmental and/or interdepartmental quality improvement activities.
9. Participate in and successfully completes Mandatory Education.
10. Perform all other duties as needed or directed to meet the needs of the department.

Key Relationships:

  • CVO Executive Director – Reports to and collaborates closely with the Executive Director of System Provider Credentialing and Medical Staff Services to implement strategic initiatives, standardize operations, and ensure alignment with system priorities and regulatory requirements.
  • CVO Manager – Maintains a strong partnership to coordinate MSSD operations with centralized credentialing functions. Works jointly to align credentialing workflows, ensure regulatory readiness, and share responsibility for the provider lifecycle and compliance.
  • CVO Database Manager – Collaborates to ensure the accuracy, integrity, and usability of credentialing data systems. Partners on database workflows, reporting, and continuous improvements that support both operational and regulatory needs.
  • CVO Staff – Partners with credentialing specialists and analysts to support the seamless processing of initial and reappointment files and to maintain readiness for regulatory reviews.
  • BILH Medical Staff Services Leadership – Develops and maintains collaborative relationships with peer MSSD leaders across the system to support consistency, information sharing, and best practice adoption.
  • Network Hospital Leadership – Serves as a key liaison to hospital leadership, supporting their oversight of medical staff governance, credentialing and privileging decisions, and medical staff-related quality and compliance efforts. Maintains a dotted-line reporting relationship to the hospital Chief Medical Officer (CMO) and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to ensure local alignment and responsiveness to site-specific priorities.

  • 3-5 years related work experience required and 1-3 years supervisory/management experience required
  • Advanced skills with Microsoft applications which may include Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint or Access and other web-based applications; May produce complex documents, perform analysis and maintain databases.

Sets up equipment for use in the work area such as, but not limited to, connecting input and output hoses, bronchoscopes, and assembling breathing circuits. title: Fee-for-Service Clinician
description:
Position Summary

The Fee-For-Service Clinician provides culturally responsive behavioral health services in both the Emergency Assistance Shelter System and a Community Mental Health Center serving the Springfield/Holyoke areas. This role involves delivering outpatient therapy to individuals, couples, and families experiencing mental health, substance use, or co-occurring disorders. The Clinician will conduct assessments, provide evidence-based counseling, collaborate with community resources, and contribute to the development of group programming based on identified community needs.

Schedule: Tues, Wed, Thurs 2p-6p (12 hours)

Pay Range: $38-$40/ hour

Essential Job Responsibilities

· Conduct comprehensive clinical assessments, develop individualized treatment plans, and provide crisis consultation as needed.

· Utilize evidence-based practices and screening tools to inform clinical work and interventions.

· Deliver individual, group, and/or family therapy using a trauma-informed and strengths-based approach.

· Complete all clinical documentation and billing records accurately and in a timely manner to meet agency and regulatory standards.

· Collaborate with shelter and community-based teams to develop and implement behavior support and risk management plans.

· Serve as a liaison with external stakeholders, including state agencies, shelters, and community providers.

· Participate in quality improvement initiatives, licensing reviews, and accreditation processes.

· Engage in ongoing professional development through trainings, conferences, and clinical consultation.

· Assist in the development and facilitation of group services aligned with the agency’s mission and the needs of the individuals served.

· Maintain clear, respectful, and culturally responsive communication with individuals, families, and collaborating agencies.

· Promote and integrate the agency’s core values and mission in daily clinical practice.

· Perform other duties as assigned by the Clinic Director.

About BestLife - Emotional Health & Wellness

The BestLife Emotional Health & Wellness Center provides compassionate, person-centered care for individuals, families, and couples facing mental health and substance use challenges. Using evidence-based approaches, our team supports both short-term needs and long-term recovery through services such as assessments, individual, group, family, and couples therapy, substance use and co-occurring disorder treatment, medication management, case coordination, and recovery support. Care is delivered by licensed clinicians and overseen by a board-certified psychiatrist, ensuring high-quality, supportive treatment every step of the way.

Equal Opportunity Statement

The Mental Health Association is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Requirements

  • Master’s Degree in Social Work, Mental Health Counseling, Psychology, or a related behavioral health field is required.

  • Prior experience working in community mental health and/or shelter systems strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated understanding of trauma-informed care, substance use recovery, and culturally competent practice.

title: Diagnostic Imaging Technologist_MIL
description:
When you join the growing BILH team, you're not just taking a job, you’re making a difference in people’s lives.

The Diagnostic Imaging Technologist performs radiographic procedures with minimal supervision in a safe, accurate and timely manner which are necessary to allow the radiologist and/or physician to make a diagnosis. Performs a variety of technical procedures requiring independent judgement, ingenuity and initiative and maintains quality consistent with established technical standards under the direction of the Chief Technologist, Chief of Radiology, Radiation Safety Officer and the Director of Radiology and Cardiology Services.

Job Description:

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Education: Graduate of a formal Radiography Program accredited by a mechanism acceptable to the ARRT (American Registry of Radiologic Technologists).


Licensure/Certifications:

· Current Massachusetts Radiologic Technologist License: Category Radiography

· Current ARRT registration (within 1 year of licensure)

· Current CEU credits, documenting compliance with CEU requirements

· BLS/CPR Certification required.


Experience: 1-4 years of Radiologic Technologist work experience preferred. New graduates considered based on strong clinical references.


OTHER SKILLS REQUIRED:

· Experience with computer systems required, including web based applications and some Microsoft Office applications including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Access. Experience with Meditech preferred.

· Ability to rely on experience, judgment and time management skills to plan and accomplish goals.

· Positive, team oriented attitude and a professional appearance.


A Physical Abilities Job Description is a component of this Job Description.


The nature of the tasks/responsibilities required of employees in this position will likely expose them to blood and body fluids. Employees will be oriented to and required to understand and to follow the universal precautions for infection control. A summary list of tasks and procedures that may cause exposure to blood and body fluids is listed on the attached Physical Abilities Job Description. Also identified is the protective gear that is available.


The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. They are not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities and skills required of personnel so classified.

Pay Range:

$35.00 - $52.01

The pay range listed for this position is the base hourly wage range the organization reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for this position at this time. Actual compensation is determined based on several factors, that may include seniority, education, training, relevant experience, relevant certifications, geography of work location, job responsibilities, or other applicable factors permissible by law. Compensation may exceed the base hourly rate depending on shift differentials, call pay, premium pay, overtime pay, and other additional pay practices, as applicable to the position and in accordance with the law.

As a health care organization, we have a responsibility to do everything in our power to care for and protect our patients, our colleagues and our communities. Beth Israel Lahey Health requires that all staff be vaccinated against influenza (flu) as a condition of employment.

More than 35,000 people working together. Nurses, doctors, technicians, therapists, researchers, teachers and more, making a difference in patients' lives. Your skill and compassion can make us even stronger.

Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled

title: Engineering Coordinator
description:
Gutor is a leading international manufacturer of UPS systems for industrial applications. The company has been in business for over 75 years and has a proven track record of delivering high-quality products and services. Gutor's products are designed to meet the demanding needs of industries such as oil & gas, petrochemical, chemical, nuclear, and transportation. The company also has a global presence with over 600 employees in more than 30 countries and branches in Brazil, China, India, Malaysia, Mexico, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and the U.S.A to name a few.

Gutor is committed to providing its customers with the best possible support. The company has a team of experienced engineers and technicians who are available to help with any problems that may arise.

The Engineering Coordinator supports Gutor’s global engineering organization by acting as a key liaison between Gutor Americas and engineering teams in Switzerland and Malaysia. This role helps ensure smooth communication, timely engineering updates, and consistent documentation throughout the life cycle of Gutor industrial UPS systems and power conversion solutions.
The ideal candidate is highly self driven, able to interpret technical documentation, comfortable with power electronics, and capable of managing engineering changes (ECOs) with precision and accountability

MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES


  • Serve as the central communication bridge for Gutor in the Americas between engineering teams in Wettingen, Switzerland and Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, ensuring alignment on technical updates, engineering priorities, and project requirements.
  • Execute local (US) engineering updates, design corrections, and document revisions “on the fly” based on guidance from global engineering leads.
  • Quickly troubleshoot and resolve minor technical or documentation‑related issues directly on the production floor to prevent delays or workflow stoppages
  • After implementing or assisting with on‑floor fixes, coordinate with engineering teams to ensure proper recording of modifications, diagram updates, and ECO documentation.
  • Review, process, and manage Engineering Change Orders (ECOs) and Engineering Change Requests (ECRs), providing structured feedback to all stakeholders.
  • Interpret and work from mechanical drawings, electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, BOMs, and Gutor’s documentation standards.
  • Support configuration management by maintaining correct revision control and ensuring that updated documentation is sent to relevant teams and production units.
  • Coordinate with engineering, production, quality, and supply chain departments to ensure technical issues are identified and addressed efficiently.
  • Identify documentation inconsistencies or missing information and escalate or resolve them proactively.
  • Work independently while managing multiple engineering tasks across different time zones.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS – REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS


  • 2–3 years of experience in electronics, electrical engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Strong ability to interpret mechanical and electrical drawings, wiring diagrams, schematics, and layout documentation.
  • Hands‑on problem‑solving skills; able to address minor engineering or documentation issues on the production floor quickly and professionally.
  • Experience with engineering documentation processes (ECO/ECR) and revision control.
  • Strong communication skills for cross‑cultural, multi‑site collaboration.
  • Highly organized, independent, and detail‑oriented.
  • The position is not eligible for employer-sponsored visa sponsorship now or in the future.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS


  • Background in mechanical, electrical, or mechatronics engineering.
  • Experience with power electronics, specifically UPS systems, rectifiers, inverters, battery chargers, or industrial power‑conversion equipment.
  • Understanding of industrial manufacturing or project‑based engineering environments.

CORE COMPETENCIES


  • Technical communication
  • Cross‑functional collaboration
  • Engineering documentation control
  • Troubleshooting and problem‑solving
  • Independence and proactive work habits
  • Ability to coordinate multi‑site engineering teams

WHAT WE OFFER


  • The base salary range for this position is $70,000 - 80,000 USD, depending on experience and qualifications.
  • Paid Time Off: 20 days of vacation
  • Paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan: up to 6% company matching contribution
  • Cigna Dental and Vision Insurance
  • FSA and HSA savings account options
  • Basic Life and AD&D Insurance
  • Voluntary supplemental life insurance
  • Health & Fitness Reimbursement


Gutor is an equal opportunity employer and prohibit discrimination/harassment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

title: System Administrator
description:
Torch Technologies

Thank you for your interest in employment with Torch Technologies. We are a 100% employee-owned, Certified Great Place To Work and named Best Places to Work in Huntsville/Madison County, headquartered in Huntsville, AL. Our team provides superior research, development, and engineering services to the Federal Government and Department of War. As one of the nation’s top 100 defense companies, the services we provide directly support the men and women who serve our country. Our corporate mission sums up the pride our employee-owners take in the work we do: “Lighting the Pathway of Freedom”. And, as a Certified Evergreen ESOP, we have made the commitment to grow and sustain our company for the next 100 years! Come grow with us!

Torch Technologies is seeking a System Administrator to join our team.


As a Systems Administrator your duties will include, but are not limited to:

  • Provide cybersecurity-focused systems administration, sustainment, and technical support for the flight’s Windows- and Linux-based data-processing, software-development, test-support, and mission-information environments.
  • Operate, maintain, troubleshoot, secure, patch, upgrade, and document servers, workstations, virtualized environments, storage, network services, and associated applications.
  • Perform system configuration; Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) compliance and security hardening; account, privilege, and access management; vulnerability scanning and remediation; configuration and change management; backup and recovery; audit-log review; incident-response support; and maintenance of cybersecurity and system documentation.
  • Provide systems-administration and cybersecurity support for Automation/Artificial Intelligence (A/AI) and Modeling and Simulation (ModSim) systems supporting the Seeker and Sensor open-air test mission. This includes standalone large language model (LLM) capabilities in air-gapped environments; GPU-accelerated computing resources; containerized applications; software libraries; automated workflows; test-support applications; and data pipelines.
  • Perform all work in accordance with applicable Department of War cybersecurity requirements, Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls, applicable security implementation guidance (including JSIG), configuration-management procedures, and secure DevSecOps practices.
  • Install new or rebuild existing servers (both physical and virtual) and configure hardware, peripherals, services, settings, directories, and storage in Windows and Linux environments.
  • Participate in the end-to-end process of obtaining an Authority to Operate (ATO) and the activities required to maintain that authority.
  • Conduct risk and vulnerability assessments of planned and installed information systems to identify vulnerabilities, risks, and protection needs tailored through the RMF; identify tactics, techniques, and procedures used by malicious actors and recommend remediation strategies.
  • Apply information security policies, methods, standards, FISMA, and NIST standards and practices to organizational information systems.
  • Perform all functional duties independently in a fast-paced environment and take responsibility for identifying, organizing, coordinating, and executing necessary tasks leading to successful accomplishment of assigned duties.

Required Qualifications:

  • U.S. Citizenship.
  • Over 3 years of systems administration experience.
  • Supporting Windows and Linux environments.
  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in a relevant field. Degree requirements may be substituted with an applicable Associate’s degree and additional years of relevant experience.
  • Must have a DoW 8140 Cyber Workforce Qualification certification (i.e., Security +).
  • Strong experience with Windows Server (2012/2016/2019/2022) and Windows 10/11 administration.
  • Demonstrated experience with STIG compliance, security controls implementation, and security incident handling per JSIG.
  • Experience supporting RMF processes and ATO maintenance.
  • Must hold an Active Secret security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with Department of War (D0W) Enterprise Networks.
  • Strong understanding of DoW Cybersecurity and Information Assurance processes; experience with secure DevSecOps practices.
  • Experience with virtualization technologies, containerized applications, GPU-accelerated computing resources, and modern system monitoring tools; familiarity with Automation/AI (A/AI), Modeling and Simulation (ModSim), or large language model (LLM) systems in air-gapped environments.



Schedule: M-F; 8-5
Work Location: Onsite
Travel: 0%-10%
Relocation Assistance Available: No
Position Contingent Upon Award of Contract: No


#LI-AH1


Benefits:

Torch Technologies is proud to offer a stable and professional work environment, a competitive salary, and an excellent, comprehensive benefit package including: ESOP participation, 401(k) match, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, flexible spending accounts, Health Saving Accounts and Health Reimbursement Accounts, EAP, education assistance, paid time off, and holidays.

title: High School Healthcare Apprentice
description:
Summary

Job Description:

High School Healthcare Apprentice

PRN


The Baptist Health Paducah's Healthcare Apprenticeship Pathway is an immersive, multi-disciplinary rotational program designed for current high school students exploring careers in medicine and allied health. Under direct, certified supervision, apprentices earn a paycheck while gaining foundational, hands-on clinical and operational skills across three distinct core roles: Nursing Assistant, Orderly, and Phlebotomy Assistant. This pathway builds transferable competencies required for long-term careers in hospital systems, long-term care facilities, and outpatient clinics.


Nursing Assistant Job Duties:


  • Activities of Daily Living – assist patients with vital daily tasks including bathing, dressing, grooming, feeding & toileting
  • Vital Sign Monitoring – Measure, record and track essential health metrics like temperature, blood pressure, pulse and liquid intake/output under nursing supervision.
  • Patient comfort – Respond to patient call lights, change linens and reposition bedridden individuals to ensure skin integrity.
  • Clinical Reporting: Document basic patient care notes and immediately notify the supervising Registered Nurse (RN) of any changes in patient condition.

Orderly Job Duties


  • Patient Transportation: Safely move patients between their rooms, treatment units, imaging areas, and operating suites using stretchers and wheelchairs.
  • Sanitation & Safety: Clean, disinfect and prepare patient care rooms, examination tables, and medical devices according to infection-prevention standards.
  • Inventory Control: Monitor, restock, and organize clinical supply closets and PPE stations across assigned units.
  • Material Courier: Deliver medical records, laboratory specimens, and pharmacy items securely to authorized departments

Phlebotomy Assistant


  • Specimen Collection: Perform or assist with blood draws (venipuncture and capillary punctures) for diagnostic tests, transfusions, or research.
  • Patient Preparation: Verify patient identity, explain collection steps clearly to ease anxiety, and monitor the patient for adverse physical reactions.
  • Lab Protocol Compliance: Match collection tubes with electronic medical orders, label vials with extreme precision, and prepare specimens for laboratory centrifuges.
  • Disposal & Safety: Maintain sterile collection zones and dispose of needles and biohazardous waste strictly according to OSHA guidelines.

Requirements


  • Must be a current high school junior or senior, maintaining a minimum 2.5 GPA.
  • Up-to-date immunizations (including TB screening and routine vaccines) and adherence to facility masking policies.

Additional Education or Certification Required Post Hire


  • Willingness to enroll in and complete a state-approved Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) course and basic Phlebotomy certification during the program.

If you would like to be part of a growing family focused on supporting clinical excellence, teamwork and innovation, we urge you to apply now!

Baptist Health is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.
