Through our unparalleled science, data, technology and laboratory network, we advance diagnostics, accelerate innovation and help address some of the world’s most important health challenges. As we shape the future of healthcare, we are leveraging advanced technologies, intelligent digital solutions and data-driven innovation across our operations to enhance how work gets done and deliver greater value to customers and patients. With our global scale and deep expertise, you’ll have the opportunity to do meaningful work, grow your career and make a real impact on people’s health around the world. Together, we’re improving health and improving lives.


Labcorp is seeking an Operations Scientist I to join our team in Indianapolis, IN.


Work Schedule - Mon - Fri (Day Shift)

title: Director of Philanthropy
description:
Title: Director of Philanthropy

Are you ready to save or heal a life?


Do you want to be the person that makes the miracle of donation and transplantation a reality? Do you want to turn tragedy into hope and healing? This is what we do every single day and we think you have what it takes.

Join a team that combines the fulfillment of an amazing mission with incredible benefits. This is not just another job or listing on your resume. Simply put, this job will change you, just like organ, eye and tissue donation and transplantation changes the lives of donor families and recipients.

Every day, the Lifebanc team gets the opportunity to change lives forever. Become a part of our family as we work toward a world where everyone in need of an organ or tissue transplant receives the healing they deserve. Come be a life saver.


What is Lifebanc?


Lifebanc, is the federally designated organ, eye and tissue recovery organization that serves 20 counties in Northeast Ohio. Put simply, we facilitate and coordinate organ, eye and tissue donation and transplantation in our community and educate the public on the importance of our mission. Our vision is pursuing a future where organ, eye and tissue donation is embraced as an honor and personal responsibility. Our mission is to save and heal lives.


Position Description:

The Director of Philanthropy serves as Lifebanc’s senior leader for fund raising strategy and revenue development and is responsible for building and leading a comprehensive fund-raising program. The Director designs and executes strategies centered on corporate giving, major gifts, social giving campaigns, planned giving, and public grant opportunities; is accountable for achieving annual philanthropic revenue goals; and develops long-term strategies that diversify charitable revenue, strengthen donor relationships, and expand Lifebanc’s funding base.


This role builds, leads, and scales the Fund-Raising Department and provides leadership for corporate partnerships and sponsorships, major and planned giving, digital and peer-to-peer social giving campaigns, government and public grants, donor stewardship, and selected fundraising events. The Director coordinates with Community Relations to support aligned external outreach without assuming responsibility for Lifebanc’s broader community engagement, education, or awareness functions.


Essential Functions:

  • Develops, implements, and evaluates annual and multi-year philanthropic strategies aligned with Lifebanc’s mission, strategic priorities, and approved financial plan.
  • Establishes fund raising goals, key performance indicators, qualified pipeline expectations, revenue forecasts, and corrective action plans.
  • Develops and maintains a compelling organizational case for support and coordinates corporate, social giving, and public grant campaign calendars.
  • Builds and manages a portfolio of corporate giving prospects and partners, including identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Develops and manages a portfolio of major donors and philanthropic prospects, leading cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and gift renewal strategies
  • Designs and executes social giving campaigns, including digital, peer-to-peer, employee, and cause-based giving initiatives, with clear participation, revenue, and acquisition goals.
  • Engages executive leaders and Board members in corporate cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and grant support activities.
  • Develops strategic relationships with corporations, foundations, government agencies, healthcare organizations, and other institutional funding partners.
  • Secures corporate gifts, sponsorships, matching gifts, workplace giving support, and other partnership revenue for approved organizational priorities.
  • Leads public grant strategy, including opportunity identification, internal coordination, application development, submission planning, award compliance, and performance reporting in collaboration with the Grant Writer and program leaders.
  • Oversees donor recognition, acknowledgments, stewardship communications, impact reporting, and other activities that support donor retention and engagement.
  • Evaluates and develops opportunities for planned giving, legacy gifts, and long-term donor engagement strategies.
  • Partners with Marketing to develop campaign content and with Community Relations to coordinate external touchpoints, avoid duplication, and maintain clear departmental roles.
  • Builds and develops the Fund-Raising Department, including defining its operating model, establishing roles and workflows, recruiting and onboarding staff, setting performance expectations, performing performance management activities, providing coaching and employee development, administering corrective action and disciplinary processes in partnership with Human Resources and leading, coaching, and evaluating team members as the function grows.
  • Develops the annual department budget and monitors performance against revenue, expense, and net contribution goals.
  • Prepares and presents fundraising performance, pipeline activity, forecast updates, opportunities, risks, and recommended actions to the Chief Financial Officer, executive leadership, and the Board, as appropriate.
  • Uses donor data, prospect research, portfolio analytics, and campaign results to guide strategy, prioritize resources, and improve performance.
  • Partners with Finance to support accurate gift processing, reconciliation, restriction tracking, financial reporting, budgeting, and audit readiness.
  • Ensures compliance with charitable solicitation requirements, gift acceptance policies, donor privacy expectations, grant and sponsorship terms, naming requirements, and organizational financial controls.
  • Develops, documents, implements, and periodically updates fund raising policies, procedures, standards, and departmental best practices in partnership with Finance, Legal, and other internal stakeholders.
  • Maintains confidentiality, integrity, and appropriate use of donor and prospect information.
  • Represents Lifebanc at donor, corporate, grantor, and fundraising meetings or events when directly connected to fund raising objectives.
  • Promotes a collaborative, accountable, ethical, and donor-centered culture throughout the organization.
  • Performs additional tasks, as needed to support Lifebanc’s mission and organizational objectives.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.


Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, business administration, communications, marketing, public administration, healthcare administration, or related field required. Advanced degree preferred.
  • Seven to ten years of progressive fundraising, philanthropy, corporate giving, grant development, or related nonprofit experience required.
  • A minimum of three years of leadership or management experience, including responsibility for building or significantly expanding a philanthropy, fundraising, or related revenue-development function, required.
  • Demonstrated success securing corporate gifts, sponsorships, public grants, or revenue through social giving campaigns required.
  • Demonstrated success achieving annual fundraising revenue goals and managing fundraising pipelines with measurable results required.
  • Experience with corporate partnerships, sponsorships, digital or peer-to-peer giving, government grant processes, donor stewardship, and fundraising events preferred.
  • Experience developing fundraising budgets, revenue forecasts, performance measures, and reports for executive or Board audiences preferred.
  • Certified Fund-Raising Executive (CFRE) designation preferred.


Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Strong knowledge of corporate giving, sponsorship development, social giving campaigns, public grant processes, donor stewardship, and professional fundraising ethics.
  • Ability to develop strategy and translate organizational priorities into clear, compelling philanthropic opportunities.
  • Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with corporate partners, grant-making agencies, donors, executives, Board members, and cross-functional colleagues.
  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Strong leadership, organizational design, hiring, coaching, team development, change management, and cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to build a department from an early stage and scale it responsibly.
  • Strong financial acumen, including the ability to develop budgets, evaluate fundraising return, forecast revenue, and interpret performance data.
  • Ability to analyze donor and campaign data, prioritize opportunities, and translate findings into actionable strategies.
  • Excellent organizational and project management skills, including prioritization, follow-through, and management of multiple concurrent initiatives.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment, initiative, discretion, and independent decision-making.
  • Ability to maintain strict confidentiality and handle sensitive donor and organizational information appropriately at all times.
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, high-accountability environment while maintaining attention to detail.
  • High proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
  • Experience with donor relationship management or fundraising database systems.
  • Ability to travel throughout the service area and attend periodic evening and weekend donor, corporate, grantor, and fundraising events.

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to lift 25 pounds and sit or stand for extended periods of time.


Compensation and Benefits:

When you join Lifebanc you can expect competitive salaries and a great benefit package. Our benefits include health, dental and vision insurance, health savings account, dependent care flexible spending account, short-term disability, and life insurance. We also offer a generous paid time off program, 401(K) retirement plan, parental leave, on-site fitness facility, tuition reimbursement and more!

Lifebanc is committed to a workforce that is diverse, inclusive and equitable. We encourage qualified candidates to apply.

title: International Admissions Counselor
description:
Reporting to a designated Undergraduate Admission leader, the International Admission Counselor is a member of the International Admission team and supports the recruitment, admission, and enrollment of prospective international undergraduate students as part of LMU's broader undergraduate admission strategy. The position provides timely, culturally responsive admission counseling and day-to-day communication with prospective students, applicants, admitted students, and families by email, telephone, virtual engagement, and in-person interaction.

The counselor manages assigned recruitment territories and activities; develops relationships with students, families, school counselors, and educational partners; participates in application review and admission evaluation; represents LMU at recruitment events in assigned international markets; and collaborates closely with the International Admission team and Undergraduate Admission colleagues to advance University enrollment goals. This role requires approximately 8-12 weeks of international recruitment travel annually, along with periodic domestic travel and evening or weekend work associated with recruitment and enrollment activities.

Position Specific Responsibilities/Accountabilities

  • Collaborate with Undergraduate Admission colleagues and campus partners engaged in international student outreach, transition, enrollment, and student-support initiatives, while referring matters outside the position's admission scope to the appropriate office.

  • Participate in domestic, virtual, and on-campus recruitment and enrollment programs as assigned, including programs that may occur during evenings or weekends.
  • Remain current on international educational systems, admission practices, ethical standards, relevant University policies, assigned markets, and technologies used in student recruitment and applicant engagement.
  • Perform other duties as assigned or requested.

Loyola Marymount University Expectations

Exhibit behavior that supports the mission, vision, and values of the university. Communicate and employ interpersonal actions that model high standards of professional, responsible, accountable, and ethical conduct. Demonstrate a commitment to outstanding customer service.

Requisite Qualifications


  • Typically a bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. The incumbent will be expected to continue upgrading knowledge, skills, and abilities to remain current with trends, technologies, ethical standards, and policy changes relevant to admission and international recruitment.
  • Minimum two years of relevant experience in admission, student recruitment, international education, student services, customer service, counseling, or a related area is preferred. Relevant internships, graduate assistantships, student employment, or comparable experience may be considered.
  • Valid passport, or ability to obtain and maintain one, and willingness and ability to complete approximately 8-12 weeks of international recruitment travel annually, along with periodic domestic travel and evening or weekend work.
  • Ability to communicate effectively and in a culturally responsive manner with students, families, counselors, colleagues, and external partners from varied backgrounds and educational contexts.
  • Strong written, oral, presentation, interpersonal, planning, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to manage time, balance multiple and changing priorities, meet deadlines, attend to detail, and work effectively both independently and collaboratively.
  • Ability to compose routine correspondence independently, exercise sound judgment, recognize matters requiring escalation, and maintain appropriate confidentiality.
  • Demonstrated computer competency and ability to learn and use admission systems, customer relationship management platforms, standard productivity software, virtual engagement tools, and web-based technologies. Experience with Slate or a comparable CRM is preferred.
  • Proficiency in an additional language and familiarity with international educational systems are preferred.
  • Commitment to ethical college admission practice, student-centered service, and LMU's mission, vision, and values.

Working Conditions

title: Systems Architect Engineer
description:
Torch Technologies

Thank you for your interest in employment with Torch Technologies. We are a 100% employee-owned, Certified Great Place To Work and named Best Places to Work in Huntsville/Madison County, headquartered in Huntsville, AL. Our team provides superior research, development, and engineering services to the Federal Government and Department of War. As one of the nation’s top 100 defense companies, the services we provide directly support the men and women who serve our country. Our corporate mission sums up the pride our employee-owners take in the work we do: “Lighting the Pathway of Freedom”. And, as a Certified Evergreen ESOP, we have made the commitment to grow and sustain our company for the next 100 years! Come grow with us!

Torch Technologies is seeking a Systems Architect Engineer to join our team. As a Systems Architect Engineer you will provide expert engineering and scientific solutions for highly complex, mission-critical technical software applications. In this role, you will deliver comprehensive systems architecture design services covering all aspects of networks, software architectures, software interfaces, and data flow architectures.


You will design, develop, and implement complex hardware, software, and database solutions, investigate advanced technical challenges, and establish end-to-end project architectures spanning development, network, and release environments. Additionally, you will lead the implementation of Continuous Delivery pipelines and drive contract deliverables, management plans, and technical briefings in close collaboration with Product Owners in a DoD operational environment.

As a Systems Architect Engineer your duties will include the following, but are not limited to:

  • End-to-End Systems, Network & Data Architecture: Provide expert architecture design services across software frameworks, software interfaces, and data flow architectures, establishing the project's overall technical architecture across network topologies, development environments, and release environments.
  • Complex Hardware, Software & Database Implementation: Design, develop, and implement complex hardware, software, and database applications, applying advanced scientific and engineering techniques to investigate and resolve complex technical requirements and system challenges.
  • Continuous Delivery Pipeline Leadership: Lead software applications supporting Continuous Delivery pipelines, driving technical execution and automation across Continuous Exploration, Continuous Integration, Continuous Deployment, and Release Management.
  • Requirements Engineering & Operational Integration: Develop, plan, coordinate, and integrate systems-related requirements to ensure technical solutions directly satisfy operational needs and evolving defense mission parameters.
  • Contract Leadership, Management Documentation & DoD Collaboration: Lead engineering team members through contract deliverables, task order reviews, management plans, and technical briefings, collaborating directly with Product Owners in a DoD environment to translate mission priorities into delivered capability.

Required Qualifications:

  • U.S. Citizenship
  • Bachelor’s degree
  • 7+ years of related experience
  • Ability to obtain and maintain Secret Clearance
  • CompTIA Network+ & CompTIA Security+ certifications

Required Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of related experience
  • Electronics Systems Technology or Avionics Systems Technology degree

Schedule: M-F; 8-5

Work Location: onsite

Travel: 20-40%

Relocation Assistance Available: No

Position Contingent Upon Award of Contract: No

title: Equipment Tech Engineer
description:
Equipment Technology Engineer, Electrode Coating

Full Time

Warren, OH


Ultium Cells Overview:


Ultium Cells, LLC. is a joint venture Lithium-ion automotive battery cell manufacturing plant between LG Energy Solution, Ltd., and General Motors. This high-technology plant is a new construction that has the latest in battery cell manufacturing technology. This $2.3 billion investment is among the largest battery cell manufacturing plants in the world. Ultium Cells produces battery cells for General Motors’ North American electric vehicle applications.

Ultium Cells’ partners include LG Energy Solution, Ltd.; the world’s largest manufacturer of automotive battery cells, and General Motors; a global company committed to delivering safer, better and more sustainable ways for people to get around.


Job Description:

This is an onsite position.

This position will be located in the Electrode Department.

This position will be part of a technical team responsible for engineering work that includes continuous improvement, investigating and troubleshooting equipment/manufacturing/facility problems, analyzing production results, implementing and improving manufacturing methods and processes, and ensuring high yield and productivity in a highly automated manufacturing environment. His/her functions will also include interaction with internal and external customers and external vendors to solve urgent and complex problems by identifying and evaluating alternatives to provide support of all in-plant production as required. Position requires some on-call support.


Primary Responsibilities & Duties:

  • An equipment technology engineer ensures continuous process improvement and maintains machines through teamwork and clear communication. Co-work with production and process engineers and relative teams for success in the team’s goals and for future opportunities.
  • Design, control, and provide modification and improvement of the equipment
  • Trouble shooting and solving problems on the chronic errors/trouble
  • Find root cause analysis and reporting of major errors
  • Monitor and ensure running machines continuously to reduce breakdown time
  • Co-creation of documentation of the all the machines - creating and updating trouble shooting, work instructions, identifying problems, providing information about the course of the machine operation/maintenance during a shift and implementing preventive solutions
  • Support for production and maintenance in solving technical problems
  • Ensure compliance to safety and environmental regulations
  • Direct and coordinate the activities of employees engaged in the production or processing of goods, maintenance and inspection personnel
  • Read and analyze charts, work orders, production schedules, and other records and reports to determine production requirements and to evaluate current production estimates and outputs
  • Practical knowledge and willingness to further develop in the area of mechanics / electrics / pneumatics and controls
  • Implements strategies to improve equipment uptime and availability
  • Machine cleaning
  • Additional duties as assigned

Education & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s Degree Engineering (Chemical, Industrial, Manufacturing, Mechanical or related), or similar required.
  • 0 -3 Years Industrial Maintenance Engineering, preferred
  • Must be able to speak and read English
  • Driven by objectives/KPI’s; consistent; and high personal ownership to upholding accountability to established standards and practices
  • Ability to use Logical thinking and decision making by focusing on identifying root cause objectively using data, analyzing production results, and following proven problem-solving methods
  • Knowledge of Mechanical/technical curiosity and mindset
  • Commitment and desire to learn our complex battery manufacturing processes with the goal of becoming a go-to resource for technical problem-solving discussions
  • Effective communication and presentation skills
  • MS Office tool-based report writing and oral communication skills
  • Ability to work well with individuals and teams across the company to achieve team goals and targets
  • Good computer, Troubleshooting, Problem-solving, Critical thinking skills
  • Ability to work well in a team environment a requirement


Total Rewards Information:

We offer market-competitive compensation including base pay and incentive compensation opportunities based on the achievement of Company goals. We offer employees paid time off to refresh and recharge. Our total rewards program is designed to enrich your life at work and includes the following benefits:

  • 100% Employer paid Medical, Dental, and Vision
  • Generous paid holidays
  • Tuition Assistance for continuing education
  • Vehicle Discount Program on General Motors branded vehicles
  • Communication Stipend for Personal Cell Phone

Annual refresher training will be completed every year after to fulfill the requirements of 40 CFR. Other training to be provided as required.

title: Student Intern Robotics and Control
description:
As Working student (m/f/d) at STILL you will be part of an unbeatable team. Your future working day will be characterized by respect, variety and responsibility. Exciting challenges await you every day. We offer you the chance to support our global Technology & Innovation team in Hamburg as a student intern.
You will support research and development activities in robotics and autonomous systems for intralogistics and work closely with colleagues in Europe and China on innovative technologies.
In the process, you will gain practical experience in software development, simulation, and testing, and support the development of the next generation of intelligent automated vehicles for business applications.

We offer:

A strong brand, a team, an excellent employer - that is STILL. For over 100 years, we have been developing the future of intralogistics for our customers with around 9,000 employees. STILL offers precisely tailored in-plant logistics solutions worldwide and implements the smart interaction of forklift trucks and warehouse technology, software, services and service. As part of KION, we operate in a strong international brand network between STILL, Linde Material Handling and Baoli. Convince yourself of a cross-brand activity with us!


Your benefits:

  • Attractive compensation package: fair pay (€1,200 per month)
  • Flexible working: 35-hour week with flexible hours
  • Discounted lunch in the company restaurant
  • Mobility allowance (transportation subsidy)

Tasks and Qualifications:

Your tasks:

  • As part of the team, you develop real-time software for mobile robots and autonomous systems.
  • In doing so, you implement algorithms for robot navigation, motion planning, and control, and test them in the system.
  • When integrating AI and machine learning techniques, you contribute ideas and translate them into robust solutions.
  • To improve interaction with the environment, you optimize perception systems based on real-world measurement data.
  • In close collaboration with hardware and software teams, you test systems and improve their performance.
  • You carry out simulations, lab experiments, and prototype tests and continuously further develop them.
  • In international R&D discussions, you contribute your perspective to the team and propose solutions.
  • You document the developed software modules and experiments in English so that the results remain traceable.

title: Junior Network Security Engineer
description:
A key objective of the position is to support the team in reducing the operational ticket backlog while maintaining service quality, security, and accurate documentation. The role performs initial analysis and troubleshooting, resolves standard and recurring requests based on documented procedures, and escalates complex issues to experienced engineers, the Network Security Architect, vendors, or service providers when required.

The position also supports platform monitoring, maintenance, lifecycle activities, audits, control reviews, documentation, and continuous service improvement. The Junior Network Security Engineer works under the guidance of experienced team members and gradually develops broader technical knowledge and operational responsibility across the Network Security & Trust service portfolio.

We offer:

1. Incident, Service Request and Change Processing – 35%

  • Process Network Security & Trust incidents, service requests, tasks, and standard changes using the designated IT service-management tool.
  • Perform initial analysis, troubleshooting, classification, prioritization, and documentation of incoming tickets.
  • Resolve standard and recurring issues by following approved procedures, knowledge articles, technical standards, and operational runbooks.
  • Support the team in reducing the ticket backlog through structured processing, regular follow-up, and accurate status updates.
  • Monitor assigned tickets and ensure timely processing in line with agreed priorities and service levels.
  • Collect relevant technical information, logs, configurations, and error details before escalating complex cases.
  • Escalate security-critical, high-impact, or technically complex issues to senior engineers, architects, vendors, or service providers.
  • Support the planning, testing, documentation, and implementation of standard and low-risk changes.
  • Participate in incident reviews, problem investigations, and root cause analysis under the guidance of experienced team members.
  • Create and maintain knowledge articles, troubleshooting instructions, and operational runbooks for recurring issues.

2. Firewall Operations and Security Policy Support – 25%

  • Support the daily operation, monitoring, maintenance, and health checking of enterprise firewall services across on-premises, cloud, edge, and industrial environments.
  • Implement approved firewall-rule, object, NAT, and security-policy changes by following established procedures and technical standards.
  • Validate requests for completeness, approvals, ownership, source and destination information, ports, protocols, and business justification.
  • Support the review, modification, deactivation, and removal of firewall rules and objects.
  • Assist with firewall rule reviews, recertification, cleanup, and policy-optimization activities.
  • Perform initial troubleshooting of firewall, NAT, security-policy, and communication-flow issues.
  • Monitor firewall availability, capacity, performance, and operational alerts and escalate deviations where required.
  • Support firewall platform maintenance, upgrades, backup and restore activities, and operational readiness checks.
  • Maintain accurate firewall configuration records, operating procedures, diagrams, and technical documentation.

3. VPN, Partner Connectivity and Segmentation Operations – 15%

  • Support the implementation, maintenance, monitoring, and troubleshooting of site-to-site IPsec VPN connections.
  • Process standard requests related to business partner, service provider, cloud, and third-party connectivity.
  • Assist with the implementation and maintenance of approved network-segmentation controls, security zones, and controlled communication paths.
  • Support NAC and microsegmentation activities from a network-security and policy-enforcement perspective.
  • Perform initial troubleshooting of VPN availability, tunnel status, encryption parameters, network-security policies, and connectivity dependencies.
  • Maintain accurate configuration, ownership, approval, and lifecycle information for VPN and partner-connectivity services.
  • Support periodic reviews, recertification, deactivation, and removal of obsolete VPN connections and communication paths.
  • Coordinate operational tasks with internal infrastructure teams, external partners, vendors, and managed service providers.

4. PKI and Certificate Operations – 10%

  • Process standard certificate requests and support the issuance, deployment, renewal, replacement, revocation, and retirement of digital certificates.
  • Support operational activities related to Public Key Infrastructure and Certificate Lifecycle Management.
  • Monitor certificate validity, upcoming expirations, service alerts, and certificate-related operational events.
  • Assist application owners, infrastructure teams, network teams, and service providers with standard certificate requests and lifecycle activities.
  • Perform initial troubleshooting of certificate enrollment, expiration, trust-chain, revocation, validation, and TLS-related issues.
  • Maintain accurate certificate inventory, ownership, lifecycle, configuration, and operational information in the designated systems of record.
  • Support the onboarding of applications, infrastructure platforms, network devices, users, and machine identities to approved certificate services.
  • Support PKI and CLM platform maintenance, control reviews, audits, backup and restore activities, and operational documentation.
  • Escalate complex issues related to PKI, Certificate Authorities, cryptography, trust models, or certificate integration to the responsible specialists.

5. Service Reliability, Lifecycle and Compliance Support – 10%

  • Perform recurring operational checks and maintenance activities for Network Security & Trust services.
  • Support platform lifecycle activities, including software updates, upgrades, configuration reviews, backup verification, and operational readiness checks.
  • Assist with monitoring service health, availability, capacity, certificate expiration, policy compliance, and operational risks.
  • Support technical audits, control assessments, evidence preparation, recertification activities, and remediation of operational findings.
  • Maintain the operational and technical documentation required for the assigned services and activities.
  • Perform assigned activities in accordance with approved security standards, change procedures, separation-of-duties requirements, and operational controls.
  • Contribute to service reporting by providing accurate ticket, incident, change, lifecycle, and operational information.
  • Identify recurring issues, missing documentation, and operational risks and communicate them to the responsible senior team members.

6. Continuous Improvement and Automation Support – 5%

  • Contribute to the standardization and simplification of recurring operational activities.
  • Identify repetitive tasks that may be suitable for templates, scripts, workflows, APIs, or other forms of automation.
  • Support the testing and use of approved automation for configuration validation, reporting, certificate lifecycle processing, and operational checks.
  • Assist senior engineers and architects with technical testing, implementation activities, and operational handover.
  • Contribute to the improvement of knowledge articles, troubleshooting procedures, request forms, and operational runbooks.
  • Participate in team knowledge-sharing, technical training, service reviews, and continuous-improvement activities.

Interfaces:

Internal:

  • Network Security & Trust team and Network Security Architect
  • Related infrastructure, network, cloud, workplace, application, and Cyber Security teams
  • IT service-management and support functions
  • Regional IT teams, system and application owners, and project teams
  • Architecture, risk, compliance, and audit functions

External:

  • Managed Network Security & Trust service providers
  • Firewall, VPN, NAC, PKI, CLM, and security-technology vendors
  • Certificate service providers and external trust-service partners
  • Security integrators and implementation partners
  • Cloud service providers and external business partners
  • External consultants and auditors where required

Tasks and Qualifications:

Experience:

  • Initial professional experience, internship experience, working-student experience, or practical training in IT infrastructure, network operations, network security, cyber security, PKI, certificate management, or a comparable technical environment
  • Basic practical experience with firewalls, VPNs, network-security controls, certificates, or IT operations is an advantage
  • Experience processing technical tickets or working with an IT service-management tool is an advantage
  • Initial experience with incident handling, technical troubleshooting, documentation, or standard changes is an advantage
  • Exposure to enterprise firewall, VPN, PKI, certificate management, CLM, or comparable infrastructure-security technologies is an advantage
  • Experience in an international or distributed IT environment is an advantage but not mandatory
  • Strong willingness to learn Network Security & Trust technologies and gradually assume broader operational responsibility

Qualifications/Specialization:

  • Bachelor’s degree or diploma in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cyber Security, Telecommunications, Electronics, or a comparable technical discipline
  • A comparable technical vocational qualification combined with relevant practical experience may also be considered
  • Entry-level certifications or training such as Fortinet Certified Fundamentals, Fortinet Certified Associate, Cisco CCNA, CompTIA Network+, CompTIA Security+, Microsoft security fundamentals, ITIL Foundation, or comparable qualifications are an advantage
  • Initial PKI, certificate-management, cryptography, or CLM product training is an advantage but not mandatory


Soft Skills:

  • Strong service orientation and willingness to support the team in reducing the operational ticket backlog
  • Reliable, structured, and accurate working style
  • Strong willingness to learn and develop technical knowledge
  • Ownership of assigned tickets and operational tasks
  • Ability to follow procedures while identifying unclear or missing information
  • Good analytical thinking and basic troubleshooting skills
  • Ability to recognize when escalation or additional support is required
  • Good collaboration skills and willingness to work with global teams and external providers
  • Clear and professional written and verbal communication
  • Strong documentation and knowledge-sharing mindset
  • Good written and spoken English

title: Donation Services Coordinator I
description:
Are you ready to save or heal a life?

Do you want to be the person that makes the miracle of donation and transplantation a reality? Do you want to turn tragedy into hope and healing? This is what we do every single day and we think you have what it takes.

Join a team that combines the fulfillment of an amazing mission with incredible benefits. This is not just another job or listing on your resume. Simply put, this job will change you, just like organ, eye and tissue donation and transplantation changes the lives of donor families and recipients.

Every day, the Lifebanc team gets the opportunity to change lives forever. Become a part of our family as we work toward a world where everyone in need of an organ or tissue transplant receives the healing they deserve. Come be a life saver.


What is Lifebanc?


Lifebanc, is the federally designated organ, eye and tissue recovery organization that serves 20 counties in Northeast Ohio. Put simply, we facilitate and coordinate organ, eye and tissue donation and transplantation in our community and educate the public on the importance of our mission. Our vision is pursuing a future where organ, eye and tissue donation is embraced as an honor and personal responsibility. Our mission is to save and heal lives.


Position Description:

This position is responsible for the facilitation of the tissue and eye donation process through interaction with hospital personnel, coroner personnel, communication with tissue processors and recovery staff as mandated by relevant federal, healthcare and donation industry standards.


Essential Functions:

· Identifies and evaluates all referrals for potential organ, tissue and eye donation as mandated by relevant federal, healthcare and donation industry standards.

· Collects and interprets patient medical and social history information provided by hospital/nursing home staff, coroners or investigators.

· Obtains and enters accurate referral information into iTransplant.

· Triages organ, tissue and eye donor referral calls, contacting the appropriate Lifebanc staff member when needed.

· Requests and accurately reviews medical charts to determine suitability based on processor criteria.

· Confidentially access and navigate various hospital electronic medical record systems to obtain pertinent medical charting.

· Appropriately pre-screen cases with multiple processors when applicable.

· Obtains releases from appropriate coroner/medical examiners and document specific samples and restrictions that they request.

· Communicates case activity to the Administrator on Call.

· Delivers a thorough and accurate report to DSC II and DSC III prior to family approach.

· Serves as the point of contact for funeral homes and Coroner/Medical Examiner offices regarding the donation status.

· Responds to audit findings and processor requests in a timely manner.

· Accurate timely completion of charting error tasks assigned in iTransplant and responds to all other inquiries from the Quality Department required for donor chart clearance.

· Performs all other job duties as assigned.


Education and Experience:

· High School Diploma required.

· An undergraduate degree, diploma, or certificate in the health field or related area preferred.

· Minimum of 1-2 years’ experience as support staff in the clinical health care field such as a Licensed Practical Nurse, EMT, Health Unit Coordinator, STNA, MA, Clinical Technician, or related experience in tissue banking.


Certifications and Licenses:

· CTBS certification preferred


Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

· Proficient use of computers, email and navigation of applications simultaneously.

· Proficient in data entry accuracy and ability to read and interpret medical records.

· Ability to assume responsibility without direct supervision, exercise initiative, and make responsible decisions under stressful conditions for a positive outcome.

· Strong listening skills and the ability to communicate effectively with a wide range of people, including medical staff, hospital personnel and donor families.

· Ability to Understand progress notes, doctors’ orders, lab results, and medication lists.

· Ability to access and navigate various hospital electronic medical record systems to obtain pertinent medical charting.


Physical Requirements:

· Ability to lift 25 pounds and sit or stand for extended periods of time.

Compensation and Benefits:

When you join Lifebanc you can expect competitive salaries and a great benefit package. Our benefits include health, dental and vision insurance, health savings account, dependent care flexible spending account, short-term disability, and life insurance. We also offer a generous paid time off program, 401(K) retirement plan, parental leave, on-site fitness facility, tuition reimbursement and more!

Lifebanc is committed to a workforce that is diverse, inclusive and equitable. We encourage qualified candidates to apply.


This position requires flexibility to work a rotating schedule that includes both day and night shifts.

title: Equipment Tech Engineer
description:
Equipment Technology Engineer - Cell Assembly

Full Time

Warren, OH



Ultium Cells Overview:

Ultium Cells, LLC. is a joint venture Lithium-ion battery cell manufacturing plant between LG Energy Solution, Ltd., and General Motors. This high-technology plant will have the latest in battery cell manufacturing technology.

Ultium Cells’ partners include LG Energy Solution, Ltd.; the world’s largest manufacturer of automotive battery cells, and General Motors; a global company committed to delivering safer, better and more sustainable ways for people to get around.

Position Description:

This position will be part of a technical team responsible for engineering work that includes continuous improvement, investigating and troubleshooting equipment/manufacturing/facility problems, analyzing production results, implementing and improving manufacturing methods and processes, and ensuring high yield and productivity in a highly automated manufacturing environment. His/her functions will also include interaction with internal and external customers and external vendors to solve urgent and complex problems by identifying and evaluating alternatives to provide support of all in-plant production as required. Position requires some on-call support.

Job Responsibilities:

An Equipment Tech. Engineer - Assembly ensures continuous process improvement and maintains machines through teamwork and clear communication. Co-work with production and process engineers and relative teams for success in the team’s goals and for future opportunities.

  • Design, control, and provide modification and improvement of the equipment
  • Trouble shooting and solving problems on the chronic errors/trouble
  • Find root cause analysis and reporting of major errors
  • Monitor and ensure running machines continuously to reduce breakdown time
  • Co-creation of documentation of the all the machines - creating and updating trouble shooting, work instructions, identifying problems, providing information about the course of the machine operation/maintenance during a shift and implementing preventive solutions
  • Support for production and maintenance in solving technical problems
  • Ensure compliance to safety and environmental regulations
  • Direct and coordinate the activities of employees engaged in the production or processing of goods, maintenance and inspection personnel
  • Read and analyze charts, work orders, production schedules, and other records and reports to determine production requirements and to evaluate current production estimates and outputs
  • Practical knowledge and willingness to further develop in the area of mechanics / electrics / pneumatics and controls
  • Implements strategies to improve equipment uptime and availability
  • Additional duties as assigned

Qualifications and Competencies:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Math, Physics, Statistics, Engineering (Chemical, Industrial, Manufacturing, Mechanical or related), or similar preferred
  • Driven by objectives/KPI’s; consistent; and high personal ownership to upholding accountability to established standards and practices
  • Ability to use Logical thinking and decision making by focusing on identifying root cause objectively using data, analyzing production results, and following proven problem-solving methods
  • Knowledge of Mechanical/technical curiosity and mindset
  • Commitment and desire to learn our complex battery manufacturing processes with the goal of becoming a go-to resource for technical problem-solving discussions
  • Effective communication and presentation skills
  • MS Office tool-based report writing and oral communication skills
  • Ability to work well with individuals and teams across the company to achieve team goals and targets
  • Good computer, Troubleshooting, Problem-solving, Critical thinking skills
  • Ability to work well in a team environment a requirement

Total Rewards Information:

We offer market-competitive compensation including base pay and incentive compensation opportunities based on the achievement of Company goals. description:

Extraordinary Care. Extraordinary Careers.

PTCB Required & TN Pharmacy Technician License


Work as a liaison between operations and clients regarding medication record-keeping and any related issues. Maintain all medication-related records for all facilities. Forward any service issues to Marketing for attention.

• Establish and maintain delivery schedule for monthly records with facilities and courier function. Print monthly records and route to courier function as needed for timely delivery.
• Generate custom reports for facilities as requested. Maintain schedule for custom monthly reports, ensuring reports are provided in a timely and accurate manner. Coordinate with data entry function to ensure drug profiles are active.
• Perform monthly review of facility profiles and update as needed.
• Maintain appropriate level of supplies inventory by reporting ordering needs to the Inventory Department

Education and/or Certifications:
• High School Diploma or GED required
• Pharmacy Technician license/certification/registration (per state requirements); National Certification preferred (PTCB)

Skills and Qualifications:
• 1+ years of related experience (advanced degree may substitute for experience)
• Advanced computer skills; pharmacy operations system experience preferred/required
• Ability to work independently and deliver to deadlines
• Ability to solve problems with minimal direction
• Great attention to detail and accuracy
• Ability to excel in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment working on multiple tasks simultaneously, while adhering to strict deadlines
• Quality minded; motivated to seek out errors and inquire when something appears inaccurate
• Working knowledge of State Assisted Living regulations and facility requirements
• Experience working with medication administration records

Work Environment:
• Ability to work flexible hours including weekends

What We Offer:

Guardian provides employees with a comprehensive Total Rewards package, supporting our core value of, “Treat others as you would like to be treated.”

Compensation & Financial

  • Competitive pay
  • 401(k) with company match

Family, Health & Insurance Benefits (Full-Time employees working 30+ hours/week only)

  • Medical, Dental and Vision
  • Health Savings Accounts and Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Company-paid Basic Life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment
  • Company-paid Long-Term Disability and optional Short-Term Disability
  • Voluntary Employee and Dependent Life, Accident and Critical Illness
  • Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts

Wellbeing

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Guardian Angels (Employee assistance fund)

Time Off

  • Paid holidays and sick days
  • Generous vacation benefits based on years of service

The Guardian Difference

Our clients require pharmacy services that aren’t “cookie cutter.” That’s why every Guardian pharmacy is locally operated and empowered with the autonomy to tailor their business to meet their clients’ needs.

Our corporate support offices, based in Atlanta, Ga., provide services such as human resources, business intelligence, legal, and marketing to promote the success of each Guardian location.

Regardless of your role at Guardian, your voice and talents matter. Because healthcare is an ever-changing industry, we encourage innovative thinking, intellectual curiosity, and diverse viewpoints to ensure we stay competitive in today’s dynamic business environment.

At Guardian, we are dedicated to fostering and advancing a diverse and inclusive workforce.

Join us to discover what your best work truly looks like.

description:
Torch Technologies

Thank you for your interest in employment with Torch Technologies. We are a 100% employee-owned, Certified Great Place To Work and named Best Places to Work in Huntsville/Madison County, headquartered in Huntsville, AL. Our team provides superior research, development, and engineering services to the Federal Government and Department of War. As one of the nation’s top 100 defense companies, the services we provide directly support the men and women who serve our country. Our corporate mission sums up the pride our employee-owners take in the work we do: “Lighting the Pathway of Freedom”. And, as a Certified Evergreen ESOP, we have made the commitment to grow and sustain our company for the next 100 years! Come grow with us!

Torch Technologies is seeking a Mid-Level Modeling and Simulation (M&S) Software Engineer to develop, integrate, execute, and analyze real-time simulations in support of Army Integrated Air and Missile Defense (AIAMD) systems. The successful candidate will be a significant contributor to the technical effort of a small team. This position is located on Redstone Arsenal in Huntsville, Alabama.

Job Responsibilities:

  • This job entails development, integration, execution, & analysis of real-time M&S products to support the U.S. Army in various lab and range venues including all-digital and Hardware in the Loop (HWIL) venues.
  • The successful candidate will design & develop simulations using tactical and simulation communication protocols.
  • The candidate will integrate simulation and tactical software changes into real-time simulations.
  • The candidate will track and resolve bugs, issues, and new capabilities.
  • The candidate will support integration, execution, debugging, and analysis in various venues including OEM facilities, government lab facilities, and test ranges.
  • Develop Virtual Engagement (VE) and other real-time simulations.
  • Integrate already-existing fire control, missile, C2 code bases into real-time simulations, and integrate these into larger system-of-system integrations.
  • Track, debug, and resolve bugs, issues, new requirements, updates, and other changes.
  • Design, implement, test, and maintain real-time software simulation models in C++ and FORTRAN.
  • Travel to support the integration, operation, and analysis of real-time simulation models into Flight Test environments.
  • Develop pre- and post-processing tools in MATLAB/python to better work with and analyze the simulation inputs and outputs.

Job Requirements:

  • U.S. Citizenship.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, a related field or equivalent experience.
  • 5 or more years of applicable progressively complex software design engineering experience.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and decision-making skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience with some of the following:
    • Modeling and Simulation
    • Realtime processing
    • 6DOF interceptor modeling
    • Patriot interceptors
    • AIAMD fire control
    • AIAMD sensors/uplinkers
  • Proficiency in C++, FORTRAN, Python, and MATLAB.
  • Ada experience a plus.
  • Familiarity with Python data science and plotting libraries (pandas, numpy, matplotlib.
  • Experience with build and meta-build systems such as Make and Meson.
  • Proficiency with Perforce, Gitlab and software configuration management best practices.
  • Familiarity with continuous integration tools and practices.
  • Analysis of simulation and live mission data.
  • Ability to read and understand design documents and Interface Control Diagrams (ICDs).
  • Must have the ability to obtain and maintain an active secret clearance.

Work Location: Customer- site

Travel: Yes, 0-10%

title: Audit Learning Director
description:
Your Journey at Crowe Starts Here:

At Crowe, you can build a meaningful and rewarding career. With real flexibility to balance work with life moments, you’re trusted to deliver results and make an impact. We embrace you for who you are, care for your well-being, and nurture your career. Everyone has equitable access to opportunities for career growth and leadership. That’s why we continuously invest in innovative ideas, such as AI-enabled insights and technology-powered solutions, to enhance our services. Join us at Crowe and embark on a career where you can help shape the future of our industry.

Job Description:

Overview:

The Audit Learning Director serves as the strategic owner of the Audit & Assurance learning portfolio. This role leads the strategy, governance, development, delivery, and continuous improvement of major learning programs, including new-hire development, leadership development, annual required training, SOQM and CPE-related learning, and audit technology enablement. The Director partners with Audit leadership, Learning Operations, National Office, Quality & Risk Management, Technology, Events, instructors, facilitators, and subject-matter experts to support the firm’s System of Quality Management, professional development, audit quality, regulatory compliance, technology adoption, and business performance. The role also oversees learning analytics, budget stewardship, resource decisions, and recommendations regarding the continuation or evolution of learning investments.

Responsibilities:

  • Establish and execute a strategic learning and development plan for the Audit & Assurance practice, aligned with the business objectives, audit quality priorities, professional standards, and firm strategy.
  • Lead the end-to-end lifecycle of high-quality audit learning programs, including needs analyses, curriculum strategy, design, development, delivery, evaluation, and continuous improvement
  • Oversee the development and governance of audit learning content by partnering with Audit leaders, National Office subject-matter experts, technical reviewers, Quality & Risk Management, and other stakeholders to ensure alignment with applicable standards, methodologies, and firm requirements.
  • Administer and oversee compliance-related learning requirements, including SOQM risks, required audience determinations, NASBA and CPE requirements, exam administration, certification communications, documentation, and compliance reporting.
  • Evaluate and assess the effectiveness of training programs through feedback, assessments, and performance metrics, making necessary adjustments to improve outcomes.
  • Lead learning investment stewardship, including budget planning, cost-benefit analysis, and recommendations regarding program continuation, expansion, redesign, or funding.
  • Translate quality trends, inspection themes, regulatory developments, and changes in audit methodology into curriculum priorities, required learning, and program enhancements.
  • Coordinate with external training providers and vendors as needed, including scope, quality, service delivery, contract considerations, and performance evaluation.
  • Foster a culture of continuous learning, professional development, quality improvement, and technology adoption across the Audit & Assurance practice
  • Lead and develop direct reports, providing guidance and support to ensure their professional development and performance.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Education, or a related field; and CPA certification required.
  • At least 8 years of experience in audit, with a strong understanding of audit processes and standards.
  • Experience leading learning strategy, program governance, compliance-related training, and investment decisions in a professional services, accounting, audit, or similarly regulated environment.
  • Experience with professional education requirements (NASBA CPA) preferred.

Key skills and behaviors:

  • Proven experience in curriculum development, portfolio governance, and training delivery.
  • Excellent communication, executive presentation, facilitation and stakeholder management skills.
  • Strong project management, prioritization and organizational abilities, with the capacity to manage multiple interdependent programs.
  • Strong knowledge of auditing standards, methodologies, professional requirements, and best practices
  • Ability to interpret compliance requirements and translate them into practical learning, documentation, and reporting processes.
  • Ability to analyze learning effectiveness, readiness, retention, performance trends, capacity, cost, and ROI.
  • Demonstrated leadership and team management experience, including the ability to influence without direct authority.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and learning management systems (LMS).
  • Working knowledge of audit technology, artificial intelligence, or technology-enabled learning and adoption preferred.
  • Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, manage ambiguity, and resolve escalations.
  • Detail-oriented with a commitment to accuracy, quality, compliance and continuous improvement.
  • Collaborative and communicative style, with the ability to build trust and rapport with diverse internal and external stakeholders
  • High level of professionalism, integrity, and ethical standards
  • Willingness to travel as required by business needs, including for program delivery and events.

We expect the candidate to uphold Crowe’s values of Care, Trust, Courage, and Stewardship. These values define who we are. We expect all of our people to act ethically and with integrity at all times.

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. Crowe is not sponsoring for work authorization at this time.

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in Product Ownership, Product Management, Business Analysis, Solution Consulting, or related product leadership roles.
  • 5+ years of experience working within Agile software development environments.

  • Experience collaborating effectively with Software Engineers, Architects, and Quality Engineering teams.

  • Experience managing dependencies, priorities, and trade-offs in complex software delivery environments.
  • Understanding of Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Planning & Scheduling, Logistics, Optimization, Industrial Software, or Enterprise Applications is highly desirable.
  • Familiarity with optimization concepts, operational workflows, or decision-support systems is considered a strong asset.
  • SAFe Product Owner/Product Manager (POPM) certification is considered an asset.
  • Passion for delivering customer value through innovative products and experiences.
  • Willingness to learn, adapt, and continuously improve in a dynamic environment.

title: Encampment Response Coordinator
description:
Summary
Under general supervision, the Encampment Response Coordinator coordinates the City’s response to and cleanup of homeless encampments across Garland. The position works closely with the Garland Police Department to remove encampments, pursues compliance for encampments on private property, tracks cleanup costs and encampment data, conducts public education and outreach, and evaluates programs and practices for improvement. The position also supports other Environmental Compliance Department projects and performs light administrative duties.

Pay Range: $55,946.07 - $71,247.18 (Depending on qualifications and experience)

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

  • Coordinates the City’s response to homeless encampments, from initial complaint or discovery through site assessment, notice, removal, and cleanup.
  • Works closely with the Garland Police Department and other City departments to plan, schedule, and carry out encampment removals and cleanups safely and in accordance with City policy and applicable law.
  • Coordinates and directs cleanup crews and contractors on site; ensures work is completed safely and to standard.
  • Pursues compliance for encampments located on private property; contacts and communicates with property owners, managers, and responsible parties verbally and in writing to explain violations, requirements, and deadlines.
  • Documents all compliance efforts on private property, including notices, correspondence, photographs, and site visits.
  • Tracks all costs associated with encampment cleanup efforts, including labor, contractor, equipment, and disposal costs, to support budgeting, reporting, and cost recovery.
  • Maintains accurate, up-to-date records and data on homeless encampments, including locations, complaints, actions taken, and outcomes; prepares reports and summaries for the Director as requested.
  • Answers questions and responds to complaints by phone, email, or in person related to homeless encampments; enters complaints into the inspection system and routes them appropriately.
  • Gives presentations to community groups, businesses, property owners, and other select audiences about homelessness, encampment impacts, and how to prevent illegal camping on their property.
  • Attends council meetings and outreach events to inform and update on encampment-related topics.
  • Researches and compares City programs, policies, and procedures with those of other municipalities; recommends improvements.
  • Identifies and recommends methods to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the City’s encampment response.
  • Works on assigned projects that may involve other areas of the Environmental Compliance Department.
  • Serves as the Department Purchasing Coordinator
  • Performs light administrative duties and other tasks as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Associate degree in Environmental Science, Public Administration, Criminal Justice, Emergency Management, Human Services, or a closely related field.
  • Minimum two (2) years of progressively responsible work experience in field operations, code enforcement, environmental compliance, public works, project coordination, or a related field. Experience must include coordinating work activities, responding to complaints, working with contractors or multiple stakeholders, or conducting field inspections.
  • An equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience sufficient to perform the essential functions of the position may be considered.

Preferred Qualifications

Education/ Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree, including 30 semester hours in any combination of courses in the following fields: environmental science (preferred), biological sciences, microbiology, chemistry, physical sciences, environmental engineering, or related fields. Additional coursework in communication skills is highly desirable.
  • Knowledge of or experience working with people experiencing homelessness or with homeless encampments.
  • Prior experience working in city government, including familiarity with municipal ordinances, departmental responsibilities, interdepartmental coordination, public complaint resolution, and local government operations

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • Knowledge of municipal code enforcement and compliance processes, including notice, documentation, and due diligence requirements.
  • Knowledge of issues affecting people experiencing homelessness, and of local social service and outreach resources (preferred).
  • Knowledge of safe work practices for handling hazardous materials, sharps, and biohazards.
  • Ability to lead, coordinate, and work as part of a team, including with police, City staff, contractors, and outside agencies.
  • Ability to communicate clearly, professionally, and with tact, verbally and in writing, including with property owners and members of the public in difficult situations.
  • Ability to speak in public and give presentations to groups of varying sizes.
  • Ability to keep accurate records, track costs, and maintain organized data.
  • Ability to apply policy and procedures in decision making and to solve problems.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and respond to changing conditions in the field.
  • Exhibits excellent and professional customer service skills.
  • Skill in Microsoft Office, including Excel, Word, and Outlook, and in using inspection or case-tracking software.

Licenses and Certifications

  • A Texas Class C driver’s license.

Must obtain the following training within six (6) months of hire and maintain it as required:

  • Hazardous Materials;
  • First Aid/CPR;
  • Needle and Sharps Safety; and
  • Bloodborne Pathogens/Exposure Control.

Physical Requirements / Work Environment

  • Must be able to lift and carry up to 50 pounds.
  • Regularly works outdoors in all weather conditions and at all times of the year, including heat, cold, and rain.
  • Work may involve exposure to hazardous materials, used needles and sharps, biohazards, uneven terrain, and potentially volatile situations; must follow all safety procedures and use required personal protective equipment.
  • Must possess mobility to work in field settings and in a standard office setting, and use standard office equipment, including a computer.

description:

title: Roofing Technician
description:
Job Description


As a Roofing Technician, you will play a vital role in the installation, repair, and maintenance of commercial roofing systems. Your expertise in roofing techniques, attention to detail, and commitment to quality workmanship will contribute to the success and reputation of our company.

Responsibilities

  1. Roofing Installation and Repair:
    • Install and repair various types of commercial roofing systems, including tile, foam, hot, built-up, and single-ply roofing (TPO, PVC, EPDM).
    • Prepare the work area by removing old roofing materials, cleaning the roof surface, and repairing any underlying structural issues.
    • Install roofing materials, such as insulation, membranes, flashings, and shingles, according to project specifications and industry standards.
    • Perform waterproofing and sealing tasks to ensure the integrity and longevity of the roofing system.

  1. Safety and Quality Assurance:
    • Adhere to safety guidelines and protocols to prevent accidents and ensure a safe work environment.
    • Follow industry best practices and company standards to deliver high-quality roofing installations and repairs.
    • Conduct quality inspections to verify that work meets established standards and specifications.
    • Identify and report any issues or deficiencies in roofing systems, materials, or installations.

  1. Documentation and Communication:
    • Complete any required paperwork.
    • Communicate effectively with team members, supervisors, and clients regarding project progress, issues, and any necessary updates.
    • Provide recommendations and suggestions for improving processes, procedures, and work methods.

  2. Safety and Professional Development:
    • Stay updated on the latest industry trends, techniques, and safety practices through ongoing training and professional development opportunities.
    • Comply with company safety policies and procedures, including wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) and following safe work practices.

  3. Additional Responsibilities:
    • Handle additional responsibilities and projects, as assigned.


Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in commercial roofing installation and repair.
  • Solid understanding of different commercial roofing systems and materials.
  • Knowledge of roofing tools, equipment, and safety practices.
  • Physical stamina and ability to work in various weather conditions.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to work with precision.
  • Effective communication and teamwork skills.
  • Team player attitude is a must.
  • Ability to climb a 40-foot ladder and lift heavy objects.
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.

description:
Labcorp is a global leader in laboratory services, providing the insights and answers that help healthcare providers, patients, researchers, pharmaceutical companies and health systems make confident decisions and improve outcomes. Through our unparalleled science, data, technology and laboratory network, we advance diagnostics, accelerate innovation and help address some of the world’s most important health challenges. Labcorp is seeking a Global Monitoring Specialist to join our team at Yeshwantpur in Bengaluru, Karnataka.

40hrs a week (Monday to Friday) in a rotational shift

title: Privacy Specialist
description:
Working at Infobip means being part of something truly global. With 75+ offices across six continents, we’re not just building technology — we’re shaping how more than 80% of the world connects and communicates.

As employees, we take pride in contributing to the world’s largest and only full-stack cloud communication platform. But it’s not just what we do, it’s how we do it: with curiosity, passion, and a whole lot of collaboration.

We operate with an AI-first mindset, embedding intelligent tools into our daily workflows to work smarter and more efficiently. Every role here benefits from and contributes to this approach.

If you're looking for meaningful work and challenges that grow you in a culture where people show up with purpose, this is your opportunity.

Let’s build what’s next, together.





What this role is all about:

The Privacy Specialist will be focused on managing and maintaining the company’s privacy policies and procedures, ensuring compliance with data protection requirements. It involves collaborating with internal teams and external partners on privacy matters, facilitating privacy assessments and audits, supporting contractual processes related to data handling, and contributing to privacy training and awareness programs. The role also includes maintaining privacy documentation, records, and internal tools to support effective privacy management across the organization.

What you will do:

• Maintaining existing privacy policies and procedures (is responsible for the revision and regular updates of privacy policies and procedures from initial assessment, drafting of documentation, tuning it with the stakeholders, up until the publication).

• Cooperating with internal stakeholders, as well as with customers, suppliers, and other partners in privacy matters and supporting internal stakeholders in the tendering and contracting process.

• Facilitating the privacy assessments and audits performed by customers, suppliers, and other partners.

• Facilitating the privacy assessments of vendors and service providers and the conclusion of data processing, data sharing, and data transfer agreements with them.

• Assisting in reviews and creating of the company’s privacy guidelines and procedures and documentation regarding data protection.

• Maintaining the Privacy department’s intranet page.

• Participating in the creation and implementation of privacy training and awareness programs.

• Assisting in maintaining records of processing activities and in administering the Privacy Department’s internal tools.

• Assisting in identifying and evaluating the privacy requirements of the company and providing advice on how to comply with them to internal stakeholders.

What makes you a strong fit:

  • You have legal or IT security background and at least 2 years of working experience.
  • You have very good understanding of data protection legislation and privacy landscape, especially GDPR and ePrivacy legislation.
  • You have general understanding of IT technologies concerning processing and storing data.
  • You have an ability to adapt fast and like working in a high-paced environment.
  • Your written/oral communication skills are excellent, and you enjoy working with multiple diverse stakeholders.
  • You’re curious and continuously expand your skills, and you are interested to learn more about business, technology, processes, law…

With internal mobility, upskilling, and mentorship, we help you shape your path. • Professional development - Learning never stops. Onboarding, mentorship, and training programs help you grow - no matter where you start. • International mobility - Ready to take your career global? Explore short and long-term opportunities in our Hubs worldwide. While some benefits may vary by location, our goal remains the same: to support your growth, well-being, and success - wherever you are.
